## Cache protocol

### REQ-PROTO-001 — HTTP cache round trip

The server shall store a blob on PUT, return the identical bytes on GET, report existence and size on HEAD, and return 404 for a key that has no entry.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: README.md "Why this exists"; docs/gradle.md; docs/docker-deploy.md "Verify it is working"; internal/server/server.go*

| AC | Given / When / Then | Verification | Blocking | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-PROTO-001-AC1 | Given a running server with an empty store; when a client PUTs a body to /some-key and then GETs /some-key; then the PUT returns 201, the GET returns 200 with byte-identical content and a correct Content-Length | http-integration | yes | approved | 1 item(s) |
| REQ-PROTO-001-AC2 | Given a stored key; when a client sends HEAD for that key and GET for an absent key; then HEAD returns 200 with the stored size and no body; the GET of the absent key returns 404 | http-integration | yes | approved | 2 item(s) |

### REQ-PROTO-002 — Request path is the cache key

The server shall treat the entire request path, with the leading slash removed, as the cache key - no path prefix exists and none is required on either side. This requirement covers only the non-reserved cache namespace: the reserved application paths ("/", /healthz, /metrics, /statusz) are outside it, their GET behavior is specified by their own requirements (REQ-OBS-001, REQ-OBS-002, REQ-OBS-003, REQ-PROTO-006), and reserved-path write handling is specified by REQ-PROTO-007.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: docs/gradle.md "trailing slash"; docs/docker-deploy.md; internal/server/server.go cacheEndpoint*

> Recorded at review (Sep 10): a PUT to a reserved path such as /healthz is currently accepted into the cache namespace while its GET answers with the endpoint response. DECIDED (owner, 2026-09-11): reserved paths refuse writes — REQ-PROTO-007 is the contract, and the server change ships in v0.2.0.

| AC | Given / When / Then | Verification | Blocking | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-PROTO-002-AC1 | Given a running server; when a client PUTs to an ordinary, non-reserved cache path such as /a/nested/key and GETs the same path; then the round trip succeeds, the same bytes are not visible under any other path, and the reserved endpoints continue to answer as endpoints | http-integration | yes | approved | 1 item(s) |

### REQ-PROTO-003 — Key validation

The server shall reject, with HTTP 400, any key whose segments are not 1-255 characters of [A-Za-z0-9._-], any key of more than 16 segments, any empty key, and any "." or ".." segment; path traversal shall not be able to escape the store root.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: docs/docker-deploy.md "Verify it is working"; internal/blobstore/blobstore.go ValidateKey*

> Recorded at review (Sep 10): Go's HTTP router redirects some dot-segment and repeated-slash paths (e.g. /a/../b, /a//b, /a/./b answer 307 to the normalized path) BEFORE key validation runs, so a helper-level test cannot stand in for this HTTP contract, and a redirect-following client may resubmit to the normalized key. DECIDED (owner, 2026-09-11): malformed keys are REJECTED with HTTP 400 through the real router — never normalized, no redirects. IMPLEMENTED (v0.2.0): a front controller ahead of ServeMux (internal/server.go newFrontController/rawPathIsMalformed) rejects a raw path with an empty, ".", or ".." segment (literal or percent-encoded) with 400 before ServeMux can redirect; verified by TestMalformedPathsRejectedNoRedirect with redirect-following disabled. A weaker check must not certify the stronger promise. AC3 (origin: advisor step 5 Oct 10): keys whose leaf starts with '..' are stored under a fixed shard; before this they failed with 500 or shared a path. No other key's on-disk path changes, so an existing store needs no migration. AC4 (origin: advisor ruling Oct 10): temporary files no longer share a name space with keys. A write goes through a temporary file in the directory `+tmp` at the top of the store; '+' is outside the segment alphabet, so no key's path can contain that name. Reconciliation removes files only there, plus leftover `.tmp-` files directly at the top of the store, where no key's path can lie (every key's path has at least two parts). A file is a blob when it is the very file its key's path opens (on a case-insensitive filesystem a shard directory keeps the case of the key that created it). Trade-off for stores written by earlier versions: files they left in shard directories are never removed by reconciliation. One that its key's path does not open is not indexed and keeps using disk until removed by hand; one that it does open (possible only in the shard `.t`) cannot be told apart from a stored key and is kept as that key: indexed, counted in the totals, and evictable like any entry.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-PROTO-003-AC1 | Given a running server, exercised through its real HTTP routing stack by a client that does NOT follow redirects; when the client requests keys containing a space, a "..", an empty segment, a 17th segment, or a 256-character segment - each in raw and percent-encoded form; then every such request receives HTTP 400 - a 307 redirect is a failure of this criterion, not proof - and no request mutates the store or creates a file outside the store root | http-integration | yes | approved | 3 item(s) |

### REQ-PROTO-005 — Body-size cap

The server shall reject a PUT whose body exceeds FSCACHE_MAX_BODY_BYTES with HTTP 413, without storing a partial entry; the default cap shall be 1 GiB.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: README.md configuration table; internal/server/server.go handlePut*

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-PROTO-005-AC1 | Given a server with a small configured body cap; when a client PUTs a body larger than the cap; then the response is 413 and a subsequent GET of that key returns 404 | http-integration | yes | approved | 2 item(s) |

### REQ-PROTO-006 — Browser landing page

The server shall answer a browser GET of the bare root with an HTML landing page (HTTP 200) rather than an error, without shadowing any cache key.

*Introduced v0.2.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: internal/server/status.go handleRoot; docs/migrate-from-bcn.md*

| AC | Given / When / Then | Verification | Blocking | Status | Evidence |

| REQ-PROTO-006-AC1 | Given a running server holding a stored key; when a client GETs / and then GETs the stored key; then the root returns 200 HTML linking /statusz, and the stored key still returns its bytes | http-integration |  | approved | 2 item(s) |

### REQ-PROTO-007 — Reserved paths refuse writes

PUT and DELETE to the reserved application paths ("/", /healthz, /metrics, /statusz) shall return HTTP 405 with "Allow: GET, HEAD" and shall store nothing: the reserved namespace is read-only, and a write aimed at it is a client error, never a silent cache entry.

*Introduced v0.2.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: owner decision 2026-09-11; resolving the reserved-path backlog entry from the Sep 10 PR 43 review*

## Configuration

### REQ-CFG-001 — Configuration surface and defaults

The server shall be configured solely by environment variables: FSCACHE_ADDR (default ":8080"), FSCACHE_DATA_DIR (default "./data"), FSCACHE_MAX_BYTES (default 0, unbounded), FSCACHE_MAX_BODY_BYTES (default 1 GiB), FSCACHE_USERNAME and FSCACHE_PASSWORD (default unset). No runtime reconfiguration surface shall exist.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: README.md configuration table; docs/docker-deploy.md "Configuration"; cmd/fscache/main.go*

> Known defect recorded at extraction, not blessed as behavior: at the extracted revision an unparseable numeric value silently fell back to the default. The fail-closed replacement is REQ-CFG-003 (v0.2.0, requirements-first).

| REQ-CFG-001-AC2 | Given a server started with every variable set to a custom valid value; when it starts; then each value is honored, observably (listen address, data location, cap behavior, auth behavior) | component | yes | approved | 1 item(s) |

### REQ-CFG-002 — Credentials are both-or-neither

The server shall refuse to start when exactly one of FSCACHE_USERNAME and FSCACHE_PASSWORD is set, with an error naming both variables.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: README.md configuration table "required together"; cmd/fscache/main.go run*

### REQ-CFG-003 — Invalid configuration fails startup

The server shall refuse to start when a numeric configuration variable (FSCACHE_MAX_BYTES, FSCACHE_MAX_BODY_BYTES) is unparseable, carries trailing garbage, is negative, or overflows, exiting non-zero with a message naming the variable and the offending value. It shall never silently substitute a default for an invalid value: a typo in a size cap must stop the server, not unbound the cache.

*Introduced v0.2.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: test-strategy.md §2.1; audit §16; backlog entry resolved by this requirement*

### REQ-CFG-004 — Configuration is validated before anything is created

The server shall validate every configuration variable, and bind its listen address, before it creates, opens, or writes anything under FSCACHE_DATA_DIR. It shall refuse to start on an invalid or already taken FSCACHE_ADDR with an error naming FSCACHE_ADDR and the value, and a refused start shall leave the data directory exactly as it found it. The listen socket is bound first and served only once the stores are ready, so connections arriving during a startup reconcile wait in the listen backlog.

### REQ-CFG-005 — Unknown FSCACHE_ variables are reported

At startup, after the configuration validates, the server shall log one warning for each environment variable whose name begins with FSCACHE_ (case-sensitive) and is not a configuration variable it knows, and shall start normally. The warning names the variable and never its value. The list of known variables is a single list in the code, kept equal to the documented configuration table.

## TLS

### REQ-TLS-001 — Optional native TLS listener

When both FSCACHE_TLS_CERT and FSCACHE_TLS_KEY name a PEM certificate file and its private key file, the server shall serve HTTPS only, on FSCACHE_ADDR. It shall use a minimum of TLS 1.2 and Go's default cipher suites. When neither is set, it shall serve plain HTTP as today. It shall refuse to start on a one-sided pair, an unreadable or unparseable file, or a certificate and key that do not match. It shall do this before it creates or writes anything under FSCACHE_DATA_DIR. The files are read once at startup; a new certificate takes effect on restart. No log line, error message, metric or status field shall contain the private key's contents.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: issue 278 (gap X2); cmd/fscache/main.go loadConfig and loadKeyPair and serve; internal/server/tls.go TLSConfig; internal/server/server.go NewHTTPServer; README.md; docs/kubernetes.md; docs/docker-deploy.md; docs/gradle.md*

> AC9 (HTTP/1.1 only with TLS on) was added at advisor step 5 on Oct 11, after the read-back: with TLS on the server negotiates only HTTP/1.1; a client offering only h2 by ALPN gets no h2 connection. The 1 MiB file-size cap (Sonnet step-8 residual R3) is in AC3's text, added at advisor step 5 on Oct 11. AC4 note (residual R2, Oct 11): Go's http.Server error log (TLS handshake errors and the like) is written through the process logger at DEBUG, so it is covered by the same capture and a flood of such errors writes nothing at the default level.

## Authentication

### REQ-AUTH-001 — Basic Auth on the cache surface

When credentials are configured, the server shall require HTTP Basic Auth on every cache request and on the status surfaces, answering unauthenticated or wrong-credential requests with 401 and a WWW-Authenticate header, and never storing or serving data for them.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: README.md; docs/gradle.md §2; docs/kubernetes.md; internal/server/server.go withAuth*

### REQ-AUTH-005 — Read-only credentials

In addition to the read-write credential pair, the server shall support an optional read-only credential pair (FSCACHE_RO_USERNAME and FSCACHE_RO_PASSWORD, default unset). Read-only credentials authenticate exactly like read-write credentials for GET and HEAD on every authenticated surface, and receive HTTP 403 with nothing stored for PUT and DELETE: developer laptops read, only the identities holding the read-write pair write. Configuration is fail-closed: the pair is both-or-neither, requires the read-write pair to be configured, and its username must differ from the read-write username.

*Introduced v0.2.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: github issue 8 "read-only client mode"; competitive-2026-09*

## HTTP

### REQ-HTTP-001 — Server timeouts

The HTTP server shall run with explicit timeouts, generous where a legitimate cache transfer is slow and tight where only a stuck or idle connection waits - ReadHeaderTimeout 10s, IdleTimeout 120s, and read/write deadlines of 20 minutes per request (enough for the documented 1 GiB body cap over a slow CI link, roughly 0.9 MB/s sustained, and finite where today is infinite). The values are configuration constants proposed by engineering on 2026-09-11 and adjustable by requirement change, not by silent edit.

*Introduced v0.2.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: test-strategy.md section 2.3; audit section 19*

| AC | Given / When / Then | Verification | Blocking | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-HTTP-001-AC1 | Given the constructed HTTP server; when its timeout configuration is examined; then ReadHeaderTimeout is 10s, IdleTimeout is 120s, and ReadTimeout and WriteTimeout are 20 minutes - none unset | unit | yes | approved | 2 item(s) |

### REQ-HTTP-002 — Bounded concurrent uploads

The server shall bound concurrent PUT processing: at most FSCACHE_MAX_CONCURRENT_UPLOADS uploads in flight (default 32; 0 disables the bound), with excess requests refused with HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header, storing nothing. Build clients treat any error as a cache miss, so a refused upload degrades a build's caching, never the build. Slow clients can therefore hold at most a bounded number of upload slots, temp files, and file handles.

*Introduced v0.2.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: test-strategy.md section 2.3; audit section 19*

## Storage

### REQ-STORE-001 — Durable storage across restart

Stored entries shall survive a clean server restart: a key stored before shutdown shall be retrievable, byte-identical, after the process is stopped and started against the same data directory.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: docs/docker-deploy.md "persistent (named volume) deployment"; docs/install.md systemd unit*

### REQ-STORE-002 — Atomic writes

An interrupted or failed upload shall leave no partial entry: a key is either fully stored and retrievable or absent, and a failed overwrite shall preserve the previous value.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: internal/blobstore/blobstore.go temp-file-and-rename write path*

### REQ-STORE-003 — Tight on-disk permissions

The store shall create directories with mode 0750 and blob files with mode 0600.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: internal/blobstore/blobstore.go dirPerm/filePerm*

### REQ-STORE-004 — A stored reply means a stored entry

A PUT shall succeed only when the blob is on disk AND its metadata record is written: if the metadata record fails, the server shall remove the blob and fail the PUT. A cache that says "stored" has stored it — retrievable, indexed, counted, and evictable.

*Introduced v0.2.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: audit-response-2026-09-08 §4.7 (decided); test-strategy.md §2.2; audit §18*

### REQ-STORE-005 — Startup reconciliation after unclean shutdown

The server shall write a marker file at startup and remove it on clean shutdown. When the marker is present at startup (an unclean exit), the server shall reconcile the two stores before serving: blobs without a metadata record are adopted (size from disk, recency now), records without a blob are dropped, stale temporary files are removed, totals are recomputed, and the reconciliation counts are logged. Blobs are truth; metadata is a rebuildable index. Clean restarts skip the walk.

*Introduced v0.2.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: audit-response-2026-09-08 §4.7 (decided); test-strategy.md §2.2; audit §18*

> AC4 added Oct 11 2026 (advisor step 5): from the Codex round-5 finding on PR #257. A startup whose reconciliation returned an error cleared the marker on the way out, although a failed start is not a clean shutdown; the behavior predates #257. The same mechanism covers a panic inside the reconcile: the marker is marked to be kept before the reconcile is called and released only after it succeeds, so a panic propagates as before and the marker stays (review residual, Oct 11; the AC text is unchanged). AC5 added Oct 11 2026 (advisor step 5): from the Codex round-2 consultation on PR #295. On a serving or shutdown error the HTTP server is closed without waiting for active handlers, so an upload can leave a blob with no index record; the marker now stays so the next start reconciles. Draining active handlers before the stores close is not part of this rule. The marker is kept on every exit except a clean return (including a panic).

## Eviction

### REQ-EVICT-001 — Size-capped LRU eviction

With FSCACHE_MAX_BYTES set, the server shall bound the COMMITTED LIVE-CACHE BLOB BYTES - the total size of indexed, retrievable entries, measured after an operation completes - by evicting least-recently-used entries; with the cap at 0 the store shall be unbounded. This is a bounded live-cache size with documented temporary headroom, not a hard filesystem quota: temporary and in-flight disk usage during writes, and concurrent-write headroom, are outside this requirement and need requirements of their own before any hard disk ceiling is claimed. That exclusion covers in-flight temporary disk usage only, never the accuracy of the index once the operations have completed (REQ-STORE-001-AC2).

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: README.md "Full core"; docs/docker-deploy.md "Sizing"; internal/cache/cache.go*

> Recorded at review (Sep 10): the implementation writes the incoming object before evicting, and an entry LARGER than the whole cap is accepted and then immediately evicted itself (write succeeds, read returns not-found, indexed total returns to zero). The oversized- entry policy is an open product decision in backlog.yaml; this criterion is therefore limited to entries that individually fit within the cap, so it describes the extracted contract without silently strengthening it. DECIDED (owner, 2026-09-11): oversized entries are rejected — REQ-EVICT-002 is the contract, and the server change ships in v0.2.0.

### REQ-EVICT-002 — Oversized entries are rejected, not churned

A PUT whose entry is larger than the configured cache cap (FSCACHE_MAX_BYTES, when set) shall be rejected with HTTP 413 and the response header "X-FSCache-Reject: entry-exceeds-cache-cap", storing nothing and evicting nothing. This rejection is distinct from the body-limit rejection (REQ-PROTO-005): a request over FSCACHE_MAX_BODY_BYTES is refused for its size on the wire and does not carry this header; a request over the cache cap is refused because it can never live in the cache, and says so. Build clients treat any 413 as a cache miss, so a build containing such an artifact completes normally without remote caching for it.

*Introduced v0.2.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: owner decision 2026-09-11; resolving the oversized-entry backlog entry from the Sep 10 PR 43 review*

## Observability

### REQ-OBS-001 — Liveness endpoint

The server shall answer GET /healthz with HTTP 200 and body "ok" for as long as the process is serving. /healthz is a liveness check only: it does not look at the data directory, the disk, or the store, so it never reports a full, read-only, or otherwise failing data directory. Operators who need to alert on disk trouble use the fscache_store_writable, fscache_store_free_bytes, and fscache_put_errors_total metrics (REQ-OBS-002).

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: README.md quickstart; docs/docker-deploy.md; internal/server/server.go handleHealthz; owner decision 2026-10-09 (backlog 13 (a)+(c)); advisor step 5 2026-10-09*

### REQ-OBS-002 — Prometheus metrics

GET /metrics shall expose, in Prometheus format, at least fscache_http_requests_total (by method and status), fscache_cache_hits_total, fscache_cache_misses_total, fscache_bytes_read_total, fscache_bytes_written_total, fscache_http_request_duration_seconds, fscache_evicted_entries_total, fscache_store_bytes, and fscache_store_entries, and fscache_store_writable, fscache_store_free_bytes, and fscache_put_errors_total (by reason). The last three describe disk trouble; /healthz never does (REQ-OBS-001). The counters shall move with real traffic.

## Privacy

### REQ-PRIV-001 — No outbound connections

The server shall make no outbound network connections — no telemetry, no update check, no licence check, no name resolution — at rest or under load, and shall run identically on a host with no route to the internet.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: SECURITY.md "Data handling"; README.md security section; www "What we do not collect"*

## Platforms and artifacts

### REQ-PLAT-001 — Binary platform matrix

Every release shall ship static (CGO_ENABLED=0) standard and FIPS-variant binaries for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. No macOS or Windows binaries are shipped; the release notes say so and point macOS users to the container image.

## FIPS 140-3

### REQ-FIPS-001 — Validated-module FIPS build

The -fips build shall link Go's CMVP-validated FIPS 140-3 cryptographic module (certificate #5247), selected at build time by GOFIPS140. Enabled mode alone is not this requirement: a standard build can enable FIPS mode at runtime (GODEBUG=fips140=on) without containing the frozen validated module, so evidence must establish the module identity, not just the mode.

*Introduced v0.1.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: README.md "Image variants"; docs/install.md FIPS section*

### REQ-FIPS-002 — FIPS posture observable and truthful at runtime

The startup log and /statusz shall report the actual FIPS operating mode and the actual module identity truthfully in every runtime configuration, including runtime overrides: a -fips build in its default runtime configuration reports active with its module identified; a standard build in its default configuration reports off; and a standard build with FIPS mode enabled at runtime (GODEBUG=fips140=on) shall not claim the validated module or its certificate. The report shall never state more than the binary can know about itself.

*Introduced v0.2.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: docs/install.md; docs/offline-install.md; internal/buildinfo*

### REQ-REL-005 — Every CI action pinned to a commit digest

Every GitHub Action a workflow uses shall be pinned to a full commit digest with its version in a comment, and every container image the pipeline names or passes to an action shall be named by digest; a tag or branch reference shall fail the check that gates every pull request. The check enforces plain forms only (owner, Oct 3): a deliberately hidden form is out of its scope; reviewers judge intent, and an obfuscation-only finding is information, not a blocker.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/agent-review-gate.yml; .github/workflows/ci.yml*

> REQ-REL-005-AC2 (the literal-label runner matrix) is advisor-approved at the read-back of Oct 9 (pin matrix): the v0.3.0 Build and Rebuild run their per-architecture apk jobs as a matrix of the two native GitHub-hosted labels, and the check accepts exactly that one expression form and nothing looser (the owner's pin-checker scope: plain forms only). The label list is closed on purpose; adding a runner label is a reviewed edit of the check. Scope: the runner rule is read in files under .github/workflows/ only. In another YAML file under .github/ a valid literal matrix reads its steps as bash, and a runs-on that holds an expression (or names Windows) only makes its steps read as pwsh (a finding of its own, no runs-on finding); any other runs-on there, self-hosted for one, leaves its steps read as bash with no finding. Duplicate keys: YAML keeps the last copy of a repeated key, and GitHub rejects such a file. A key given twice in a job (a job that calls a reusable workflow included), in its strategy or in its matrix is refused with the key named, whatever the last copy holds. Refused forms of REQ-REL-005-AC2, each a finding that names the runner: - any other expression or text in runs-on (text before or after the expression, a second expression, a block scalar's trailing newline, braces without spaces), a runner from an input, env or vars, an array index or property of the matrix key, a runs-on list; - a matrix that is an expression or fromJSON, a matrix of only include or exclude, in any letter case, a second matrix key, an extra strategy key (fail-fast may sit beside matrix only as the plain unquoted literal true or false, not a quoted or tagged string), a strategy with no matrix key, a key given twice in a job, in its strategy or in its matrix (the finding names the key); - a label not on the two-label list (another case or version, ubuntu-latest, a larger runner, self-hosted, macOS or Windows, a space around a label, a trailing newline, a look-alike character, an explicit YAML tag other than str; !!str resolves to the plain string tag and is accepted), a nested list, a non-string label, an empty list, a scalar instead of a list, a duplicate key; - a matrix key that does not exist or is defined on another job or at the workflow level; - and a matrix reached through a YAML anchor (the check refuses a file that holds any anchor or alias, whatever it anchors). Explicit YAML tags: any explicit YAML tag on the matrix path (the job, its runs-on, its strategy, the matrix, a key in them, the label list, fail-fast) is a finding that names the runner, even a tag that names the node's default type such as !!seq or !!map; the one exception is !!str on a label (above).

## DEP

### REQ-DEP-001 — Dependabot majors are judged by a machine

A Dependabot major version bump shall be judged by the Dependabot reviewer, not by a person: from main, hourly, it gathers the evidence with no model involved, has two readers rank findings without a verdict, and decides mechanically to merge or to hold with an issue; it posts its result as a check and edits nothing.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/dependabot-reviewer.yml; bin/dependabot-reviewer.py*

| AC | Given / When / Then | Verification | Blocking | Status | Evidence |

| REQ-DEP-001-AC2 | Given an open Dependabot major with no verdict yet; when the reviewer runs; then it gathers, with no model involved, the PR diff, the upstream release notes for every version between old and new, and every line in our workflows and modules that uses the dependency; a read of release notes or usage that fails is labeled unavailable in the bundle and is an error (no verdict, retried), never "none found" | unit |  | approved | 2 item(s) |
| REQ-DEP-001-AC3 | Given the gathered evidence for one major; when the two readers answer; then the bundle reaches two readers through the same workload-identity federation the auditor uses, with model identifiers only in environment secrets; each returns findings ranked "breaks us", "check" or "noise", never a verdict; an answer that is malformed, cut off or declares failure is an error, never a clean pass; no model name or identifier, in any letter case, reaches a finding, an issue or the uploaded evidence, the evidence bundle included | unit |  | approved | 2 item(s) |
| REQ-DEP-001-AC4 | Given both readers' findings; when the reviewer decides; then the decision is mechanical: no "breaks us" from either reader, with the required-check guard matching, arms squash auto-merge, which merges only once every required check is green; any "breaks us" from either reader holds the PR, even when the other reader errored, with one issue carrying the readers' findings and the fix, which is ccode's; a reader error with no "breaks us" leaves no verdict and is retried next hour | unit |  | approved | 1 item(s) |

### REQ-REL-009 — Automatic patch releases

Fix-only changes on main shall be released automatically as vX.Y.(Z+1): cut at once for a critical or high fix, otherwise at most once a day, signed keylessly by release.yml's own identity, run through the full release chain, with generated notes, VEX updated, floating tags moved by the owner's rule, and a failed stage abandoned without retry. Minor and major releases stay the owner's.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/release.yml; .github/workflows/stage-admission.yml*

> AC14 (origin: advisor step 5 Oct 11, owner rule 5 engineering AC): the refusals protect AC8's owner sentence (rule 5, ops/docs/ratify/2026-10-02-automatic-patch-releases.md) and leave AC8's text untouched. No line is exempt (advisor decision Oct 11, option A, replacing the round-9 VEX-section exemption): the refusals apply to every line of the changelog inputs and a generated tag's notes, a '### VEX' section's lines included. To keep the generator's own notes readable back (notes, then the tag, the changelog's notes and later the history), _lit's quoted form writes '<' and '&' as \u003c and \u0026 (the same JSON string, as a hyphen before four more is written \u002d), so no printed VEX value holds a refused form; a reader sees the JSON string (a statement named <b>x shows "\u003cb>x" in its code span); the value is redacted as text before it is encoded (an escape ends in a letter or digit and would erase the word boundary the redactor reads: '<google', '&o1'), and a statement whose CVE name or @id redaction changes is named by its position. A VEX value (a CVE name, an @id, a product or subcomponent @id or identifier, a field name) that holds a redaction-marker form ('<redacted>' or '(redacted)' in any case, as written, Markdown backslash-escaped, JSON-escaped or as HTML character references, each read once) is refused before any redaction, naming the document, the statement and the field (exit 2, no notes, no patch); a value is never converted into the marker (advisor narrow cut, Oct 12). Exotic nested spellings of the marker in a VEX field (percent-encoded, fullwidth, nested or mixed escapes) are not decoded; the refusal covers the forms our printer and readers recognise (advisor cut, Oct 12, Codex #300 b12). notes() checks its whole text, and every line, a VEX line too, is printed and read back by the one function _clean_free (a VEX line holding the redaction marker is written in the escape-whole-line form). Each line of a multi-line source value is checked before the value is made one line, and the whole go.mod line a Go fix's version is read from. go.mod is read by a strict parser of its grammar (Go's modfile lexer: '//' comments, 'verb (' ... ')' blocks): the versions and the line judged come from one parse of the require directives only (never a comment, replace or exclude line), and anything the parser does not read (a '/* */' comment, a quoted string, a control or other space character, a module required twice, a require that is not a path and a semantic version, an unclosed block) is refused, naming go.mod:line; Go is not on the decide job's PATH, so the parser is in the script. Versions are read as golang.org/x/mod/semver reads them (vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+BUILD], ASCII digits, no leading zero, no empty identifier), the go directive as a Go release version (1.21, 1.21.0, 1.21rc1), and every supported directive in its own shape (module, toolchain, require, exclude, replace, retract, godebug, tool, ignore); the name 'stdlib' is reserved for the toolchain and refused in any directive, and a stdlib fix is compared with 'go' + the go directive's version. Documented limit (advisor, Oct 11): a quoted path, which Go accepts, is refused (fail closed): the parser reads the go.mod forms the repository's go.mod files use. A fix record is judged on the scan match that produced it (the first match HEAD fixes, variants sorted, document order: the one fixed_findings prints from). The collision check (5) is one set across every published line (fix, VEX and behavior); a fix record is named by its scan file and key path; in the readers (a tag's notes, the changelog's notes, the history) two '- ' lines of one release block that publish the same line once cleaned as published ('- gpt' and '- claude'; a marker line and its escaped spelling) are refused, both named by their source lines; the same line in two release blocks is not a collision. In a generated patch tag (release tagger, gitsign signature last, heading naming the tag) a '-----BEGIN ' anywhere before that last signature is refused (exit 2, the line named); any other tag exits 1 as before. Beyond the four forms, a free-text line holding the redaction marker that continues the line above it (neither blank nor a heading) is refused in tag notes and changelog inputs (a construct spanning lines could hide the marker); --published (every v* tag message and CHANGELOG.md) is not a source and is not checked for '-----BEGIN ' (each tag message carries its signature block). 'Letter' after '<' is any Unicode letter. For a value inside a JSON scan file the message names the file and the JSON key path instead of a line. 'Already published' is decided by whole line, never substring: an entry counts as published only when a whole line of the published text equals its published line, both compared without trailing whitespace (git's tag-message cleanup strips trailing whitespace; leading and interior whitespace stay significant). tag-notes exits 2 on a refused form like notes and changelog. The code reads the reference-definition shape also after any list or quote markers and any indentation, and refuses a '[' label left open at the line end (a definition can open inside a list item; wider than CommonMark, fail closed). No published text ever held a redaction marker form other than the current one (no CHANGELOG.md on main, no v* tag message holds 'redacted'), so the marker handling is the escape-whole-line rule only.

### REQ-REL-011 — A job that holds a credential never compiles, and each build is its own job

A workflow job that holds a credential (a secret, an environment, an id-token or packages write grant) shall not build or compile anything, and no job shall run two builds: on GitHub-hosted runners the separate job is the isolation unit, each job a fresh virtual machine. Owner, Oct 21 2026 (ops/docs/ratify/2026-10-21-signer-builder-separate-jobs.md): "the signer and the builder need hardware isolation and the builds in general need hardware isolation ... the best github actions can do for that, assuming we use github hosted runers, is to use separate jobs in the workflow." The rule: a job that holds the signing key or any publish credential never receives a build output other than the exact artifacts it signs or publishes; the Rebuild comparison runs in a job with no secrets and no publish permission; builds are isolated from each other the same way, each build its own job.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/auditor.yml; .github/workflows/go-freshness.yml; .github/workflows/stage-verify.yml; bin/job-isolation-test.sh*

> Four jobs of the release chain on main (stage-build, stage-image, stage-promote, stage-reproducibility) still break AC1 and are listed exclusions in bin/job-isolation-test.sh with their reason: the chain-v030 landing (handoff 0634, cache#514) replaces those files. The exclusion list shrinks to nothing then. A tool that publishes no release binary (govulncheck) is built in its own job that holds no credential and reaches the credential-holding job as an artifact whose sha256 equals the build job's output.

### REQ-REL-012 — A pull request into the release carries a passed-audit record for its exact head

A pull request into the release carries a passed-audit record for its exact head, or it cannot merge (release process rule 6, owner RATIFIED Oct 23 2026, ops/docs/ratify/2026-10-23-release-process-features-sections-audits.md: "once we agree on this if it can be coded it should be"). The release is main. The record is the branch audit/<head sha>: one commit whose only parent is that head, verified by GitHub, authored by a writer named in .github/policy/audit-writers.json of the base checkout, adding only the file audit-record, which is the record itself. Nothing is stored in the pull request's own files, and a new push changes the head sha, so an earlier record no longer applies. The verdict is part of the existing auditor-review-gate (agent-review-gate.yml): main's copy of the judge runs over the head, so a pull request cannot edit or skip it, and a retarget re-runs it.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/agent-review-gate.yml; bin/audit-record-judge.sh; bin/audit-record.py; .github/policy/audit-writers.json*

> No new required check: auditor-review-gate is already required on main, so once this lands every pull request into main needs a record. It therefore lands only after the writer (a later pull request) and the dispatch that calls it exist, on the landing day, together with the ruleset rule that only the writer creates branches under audit/** (the owner's step). The record commit adds one file, audit-record, because the API can only make a commit that changes something.

### REQ-SCAN-010 — VEX in three forms

Every release shall publish the VEX three ways, all generated from the one OpenVEX file: OpenVEX, an Amazon Inspector suppression-rule file, and CSAF 2.0, covering exactly the same statements.

> AC5: the digest file has two variants, production and fips (v0.3.0 ships no :debug image). AC6: "repeats a key" needs an explicit check, because Python's json.load keeps the last of two equal keys and says nothing. AC7: the variants are walked in a fixed order and the children in a fixed order, so the key order of the digest file does not reach the output. AC8: the test no longer reads stage-promote.yml step names; AC3's check reads main-candidate-rescan.yml contents, not step names.

### REQ-SCAN-015 — The scanner cloud identities cannot be reached through a caller

The two workflow files that carry the scanner cloud identities (scan.yml and main-candidate-rescan.yml) shall never be callable as reusable workflows, because the cloud trust is pinned to the file and not to its caller: neither declares on: workflow_call, and no workflow or action references either one in a uses:.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/scan.yml; .github/workflows/main-candidate-rescan.yml; bin/scan-no-workflow-call-test.sh*

> AC3's last clause (reworded, advisor-accepted Oct 13, outbox note 2026-10-13-pipeline-req-scan-015-ac3-clause.md; it formerly required a review record bound to the script's content) names a review that this repository's gate does not judge as a record: the trusted verdict auditor-review-gate (agent-review-gate.yml, always the default branch's copy) runs main's pin checker, allowlist guard, pin-wiring judge and this scanner guard over the head as git objects and judges no review record (the record mechanism was retired with the gate rewrite, cache#303). The second review that a change to bin/scan-no-workflow-call-test.sh needs is enforced outside this repository by the private review tooling before merge (the same reading as REQ-AUD-018 AC3); that the main branch ruleset REQUIRES the check is not checkable from the repository and is an inspection item for the owner's settings. The guard rejects a repeated mapping key and any file it cannot read as one workflow document (fail closed), because a later key would otherwise hide an earlier declaration.

## SUP

### REQ-SUP-001 — Actions supply-chain checks

Our workflows shall take no new version of an action, or of a tool, image or package they download, until it has been public 7 days; shall check every version we use, every day, against the public advisory and malware lists; and shall say publicly only what they know.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/supply-chain.yml; .github/dependabot.yml; .github/supply-chain-exceptions.json*

> AC14 design decision (Codex round 1, B2): a non-plain version of a table tool is a HIT only on the records the databases return for it. A version with no OSV record and no GitHub advisory (cosign@latest, or the (default) pins of cosign and kind in the real tree) reads clean, deliberately: with no record nothing is known to be affected at any version, and making every non-plain pin a hit would open a daily issue forever with nothing to report. The rule is about the verdict on records, not about the pin. AC14 evaluation: range events are evaluated as OSV evaluates them: sorted by version (introduced 0 is the minimum, at one version the fixed wins), last_affected inclusive; Go versions compare as strict semver (pseudo-versions, numeric pre-releases and +incompatible are valid; r1, p1, post1 and rev1 are pre-release identifiers). A limit event is refused in SEMVER and ECOSYSTEM ranges (the record is a hit, a fail-closed refusal): the Go vulnerability database never writes limit, the OSV schema text could not be consulted offline, so any use of it in a Go range is treated as unreadable, which also removes the any-or-all question for several limits (the evaluator, used for other ecosystems, reads below ANY limit as affected). The schema asks for id and modified on a record, ecosystem and name on a package, an introduced event in every range (their order is free), and not both fixed and last_affected in one range; aliases may be absent or null. An independent interval oracle in the test compares the evaluator on a generated grid. The 240 recorded verdicts did not change. AC14 residual: the rule judges the OSV record's affected entries only; GitHub's ranges are read as before. An OSV answer that is not a record (not an object, no string id or modified) is a hit under the id UNREADABLE-OSV-RECORD; a GIT range together with a SEMVER or ECOSYSTEM range in one entry is a hit in every branch. The gh and git calls of pin-audit.py and of the shared helpers in pin-age-check.py have a 120 s timeout that stops the run (exit 2). AC14 residual (semver): bounds that SemVer 2.0.0 forbids (a numeric pre-release identifier with a leading zero such as 3.0.0-01, an empty identifier in the pre-release or the build metadata) are unparsable and read as affected, so the record is a hit. Go pseudo-versions with a zero-time stamp (0.0.0-00010101000000-000000000000) are one valid alphanumeric identifier, because it contains a hyphen, and parse normally. AC16/AC17 history: the AC16 and AC17 first accepted for this requirement (a lexer telling text from commands, pull request 272, closed: an open-ended class) are WITHDRAWN; the AC16 above replaces both, and there is no AC17 (the gap is deliberate). AC18 (literal downloads in install-build-tools.sh) belongs to pull request 271. AC16 design: the scan stays strict. A row is {file, form, key, line, ruling} plus an optional count (default 1): key is the scan's own 64-hex sha256 prefix (for a download, of the one command segment that names curl or wget), and line is the 64-hex sha256 prefix of the WHOLE whitespace-flattened line that segment sits in (Sonnet, pull request 273 round 1: a segment hash alone ruled the same segment inside another line that pipes it to sh); an item is ruled only when every occurrence in the head sits in a line a row names, and a row covers at most count occurrences of that line, so a second copy of a ruled line fails unless the row counts it. Editing the line other than in spaces and tabs (which the scan normalises) voids the row; changing only a row's ruling prose does not void it (the prose is the reason, not the identity). An occurrence is ADDED when the head has more of its (file, form, key, whole line) than the base (Codex, pull request 273 round 2: counting by key alone let an edit that kept the download segment, such as a ruled echo rewritten to pipe into sh, pass as no addition); a replay of the 150 first-parent commits of main from 7c6077b (Sep 11) to 09b30af (Oct 10) found no commit that this newly fails. A row never matches a line holding whitespace other than a space or a tab, or a line joined from a backslash-newline continuation: bash reads those differently from the flattening (Sonnet R1); count is at most 100. Intended: editing only a row's ruling prose does not void it, and a space- or tab-only edit of the line stays ruled. The exceptions file must be strict JSON: NaN, Infinity and -Infinity (which Python's reader accepts) and a repeated key stop the check (exit 2). AC16 delta accepted by the advisor Oct 10 (Codex round 3, P7): the given names the command hash (key) and the whole-line hash (line); the then states the count limit and the edited-line, whitespace and continuation failures. Limit of line identity (Codex round 3, P4; the coordinator's decision, Oct 10): shell CONTEXT is not part of a line's identity, so moving a line out of a heredoc (above its opener) or commenting the opener out keeps (file, form, key, line) and is no addition. Therefore a row is only ever written for a line that is HARMLESS IN ANY CONTEXT: read as a shell command it runs no download (a comment, an echo or printf, a cat into a file, Python source or a package list that bash cannot parse), and the advisor reviews each row for exactly that; a row for a line that would download when run is the reviewer's to refuse. The test holds the text of each committed row's line and checks it is harmless that way. Allowed row forms (advisor, Oct 10; the reviewer refuses any other row): (1) TEXT lines: a comment, a quoted or echoed string, a data heredoc (a stub body or its opener), Python or package-name text that bash cannot parse; (2) HARNESS ASSERTION lines, whose whole grammar is the single data structure HARNESS_WHITELIST in harness_form.py (written by the pin-age check's own test suite); anything it does not name is refused. In short: t "RULE" "TITLE" bash -c 'BODY' _ followed by at most nine path arguments "$NAME" or "$NAME/path" with NAME in work, CALLS; no expansion of any kind in RULE or TITLE (no $, backtick, backslash or quote); the body SINGLE-QUOTED (Codex, pull request 289: a double-quoted body let the outer shell splice a variable's value into the code) and naming the paths only as whole "$1".."$9"; the commands grep, test, [, cat and exit with one digit; grep in the shape grep OPTION... -- PATTERN ["$N"...]: the options -E, -q, -v and -Eq as bare words, -- REQUIRED before the pattern, the pattern a double-quoted word that does not start with - (or the bare '.'), file operands only "$N" (Codex and Sonnet, pull request 289 round 3: a double-quoted word in an option position is an option to grep); cat only as cat -- "$N"; test and [ only the file tests -f -s -e -d -r on a positional "$N" (never a literal path or a substitution: Codex, pull request 289 round 6), = and !=, and count comparisons between digits and "$(grep -c ...)" (never -v, -R or an arithmetic operand that is a name or expression: bash 5 evaluates $(...) there); the substitutions "$(grep -c OPTION... -- PATTERN "$N")" and "$(cat -- "$N")" only; no unquoted glob, brace, subscript or expansion word; and no character outside printable ASCII and tab (Sonnet, pull request 289). The test proves the whitelist closed: a complement enumeration of every token class outside it in every position (none accepted, none refused for another reason), and a mutation run that widens it by one token at a time and requires an unexpected acceptance or a refusal for another reason (reported apart). The role rules that live in the parser's code (a file test on a positional, cat with exactly one operand, a positional within the arguments) are pinned by code mutants that loosen each one and must be caught. A harness line that reads a test stub's call log matches whole ROLE-TAGGED fields of a log the stub writes from its own parse (opt, val, out, url, unk; brackets inside a word become _), never substrings of flattened text (Codex and Sonnet, pull request 289 round 4); the later rows pull request runs each such line against logs with the right words in the wrong roles, forged fields inside URLs and -o values imitating flags. Scope (coordinator, Oct 11): this pull request carries the FORM (the parser, HARNESS_WHITELIST pinned by its golden canonical sha256, the complement enumeration, the mutation run, the runtime corpus with synthetic lines in the shapes of the input refresh assertions) and the three comment rows; the rows for the input refresh harness lines, with the test of what each line asserts, come with those lines in a later rows pull request. HARNESS_WHITELIST is pinned by HARNESS_WHITELIST_GOLDEN in the test: any change to the grammar needs that value edited in the same reviewed diff. The test decides form (2) with a quote-aware parser (harness_form.py in the test) and proves each refused variant as its own case. The rows are read from the exceptions file beside the checkout the script runs from (in CI trusted/, the base branch), never from the pull request's tree; a missing default file is no rows; a malformed list (not a list, a row that is not an object, a missing, empty or extra field, a key or line that is not 16 lowercase hex, a JSON object that repeats a key, a count that is not a whole number from 1 to 100, a repeated row) stops the check with exit 2. AC15 limit: the pins nested inside an action are not counted as held, so a ruling for a pin that is only nested can be dormant, never dead. AC15 expectation (step 8, Oct 9): the three cosign rulings (GO-2024-2718, GO-2024-2719, GO-2023-2181) are ALIVE now because main pinned cosign 3.1.3 inside the 90-day history window (until commit 8a7512d); they become dormant (or dead, if a cosign 3.1.3 pin has appeared and they decide nothing) about 2026-12-14, 90 days after that pin left main, unless a cosign 3.1.3 pin is held again (pull request 249). Finding at step 6 (Oct 9): with the corrected table paths, the existing package-name filter of the audit already clears cosign 3.1.3 against GO-2026-4309. The real work of AC14 is (1) the corrected table (goreleaser, osv and golangci-lint need their /v2 path), (2) GitHub names matched under both the bare and the /vMAJOR path so the five existing rulings keep working, (3) the log of ignored entries, (4) the OSV query by the /vMAJOR path.

## UAT

### REQ-UAT-001 — Persona UAT

Five agents, each playing a different customer and reading only our public documents, shall exercise every release candidate and the latest release every week, the way a real acceptance test would.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: bin/persona-uat.py; bin/persona-uat-agent.py; .github/workflows/release.yml; .github/workflows/go-freshness.yml*

## REPO

### REQ-REPO-001 — Branch hygiene without a human

The repository shall remove its own stale branches with no human step and never remove a good one: a daily sweep deletes a remote branch whose pull request is merged or closed, or that has no pull request and no commit for 14 days, and never touches the default branch, release branches, Dependabot branches, a branch with an open pull request, a branch that is the base of an open pull request, or a branch kept by an unexpired entry in a keep-file on the default branch; every deletion is logged with its commit so it can be restored; and a local script prunes the lane's own stale local branches and worktrees without losing work.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/reserved-branch-guard.yml; bin/branch-sweep.py; bin/local-prune.sh; .github/branch-keep.json*

> The sweep is a scheduled job inside the existing reserved-branch-guard workflow (no new workflow file). Its planner is bin/branch-sweep.py; the keep-file is .github/branch-keep.json, an object {"keep": [{"branch", "expires" (YYYY-MM-DD), "reason"}]} read through the API at the default branch. The sweeper reads the runner's response headers by lower-case key (link). Local prune finds gone branches in a dry run with git ls-remote --heads origin (read-only); only --apply may run git fetch --prune. Branches on forks are out of scope.

## CHAIN

### REQ-CHAIN-001 — The Sign job is its own workflow file and cannot be reached from Build

The release provenance shall be written and signed keyless by a Sign job that lives in its own workflow file, runs on its own fresh GitHub-hosted runner, never runs code from the build, receives only Build's digests, Build's and Rebuild's local Witness records and the exact artifacts those records name (all as data, never executed), signs the release provenance and, after checking them, the Witness records of Build and Rebuild, and whose signing identity no other job can obtain, so that a malicious Build step cannot produce provenance that Release accepts (SLSA Build Level 3 design).

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/stage-sign.yml; .github/workflows/release.yml; bin/chain-verify.py; bin/chain-hostile-step.sh; .github/policy/chain-signers.json; .github/policy/chain-scripts.json*

> stage-sign.yml is the one new workflow file v0.3.0 adds (rule 52). PR 1 builds the Sign side and the verify side; Release's own signing of the policy (rule 57) is PR 4. Public copy says "designed to SLSA Build Level 3", never "certified" (rule 50a, 84). REQ-REL-008-AC1 changed from 25 to 26 files because rule 52 ratifies exactly one new workflow file, stage-sign.yml (owner RATIFIED Oct 9 2026 11:51 EDT, ops/docs/ratify/2026-10-09-v030-rules.md). Step-8 round 1 (Opus and Sonnet, advisor 0343 process): the hand-code attempt of the dry run uses `chain-verify.py check-build-record` (the same refusals as `sign --check`, no signer, no cosign), so no job other than stage-sign.yml names the signing subcommand and the earlier exemption for jobs without id-token is gone; a workflow_dispatch on a TAG is refused by `sign --check` and the hostile input is limited to a branch ref (`inputs.dry-run == true && github.ref_type == 'branch'`); the build call of a dry run runs in snapshot mode (admission is skipped on a manual run, which used to skip build, sign and both hostile jobs), publishes no GitHub attestation and needs no admission artifact. RUNTIME PROOF OF AC5 (advisor accepted Oct 10 (lane AC); moved by the accepted text of Oct 12): the runtime proof is the signed release-candidate tag run on main, cut after the cutover pull request has merged (advisor 0383); no GitHub dry run in a pull request is part of it, and the sixth case is judged by Sign's caller check in the static judge and by the offline hostile test. CUTOVER CHECKLIST (order accepted Oct 12): (1) the cutover pull request (chain-v030 to main) merges with every known-red entry but KR-CUTOVER gone (bin/chain-known-red.py empty-except KR-CUTOVER), every hosted check green on hosted runners and the review records bound to its tree; it does not wait for an rc run (admission requires the tagged commit to be on main), and the one entry KR-CUTOVER stays, meaning 'rc proof pending'; (2) the owner signs a release-candidate tag vX.Y.Z-rcN on main's merge commit; its run is the REQ-CHAIN-001-AC5 GitHub proof (the hostile jobs, Sign, Rebuild, Check and Release's release-verify, which ends a release candidate), and one genuine cosign v3.1.3 bundle from it passes `chain-verify.py verify` (the Rekor inclusionPromise question of REQ-CHAIN-002); (3) the marker pull request of REQ-CHAIN-001-AC6 (.github/policy/rc-proof.json and the removal of the one KR-CUTOVER entry from test-evidence/known-red.json, nothing else) follows the first green rc run at once; its CI verifies that run's records with `chain-verify.py rc-proof`, and it removes KR-CUTOVER (bin/chain-known-red.py empty: the list is then empty); (4) until that marker is on main, admission and the patch decide job refuse every final and patch tag, so no v0.3.0 and no automatic patch runs the chain before its own rc proof. THE MARKER PULL REQUEST'S GATE (slice 4b-6, orchestrator Oct 13): the job marker-gate of ci.yml, run by bin/marker-pr-gate.py from the base checkout, stops a marker pull request that carries anything but the marker and the removal of KR-CUTOVER, or that names a run that does not verify under `chain-verify.py rc-proof`; a pull request that also rewrites that job is stopped by the workflow-change rule (both reviews and the owner's merge), not by the job itself. Dry run (pipeline design, round 5-6; advisor to confirm): on a workflow_dispatch on a branch Sign writes a record marked dryRun and its SAN ref is the branch; such a record can only be judged under a dry_run policy by the dry run's own verify job (stage sign only), while Release makes its policy with --tag, every stage-start refuses a dry_run policy, and a provenance carrying dryRun true is refused under any non-dry policy; the jobs after Sign carry no tag-ref conjunct of their own (release.yml's image to promotion jobs have only `!inputs.dry-run`): the tag guard reaches them through needs, because build requires admission.result == 'success' outside a dry run and admission runs only on a v* tag (bin/chain-sign-wiring-test.sh, case R8).

### REQ-CHAIN-002 — Timestamps, the transparency log and the per-tag release policy

Every keyless signature in the release chain shall carry Sigstore's public timestamp so it can be checked after its ten-minute certificate expires, everything a customer verifies shall have an entry in Rekor, and each tag shall have a release policy made from a committed template that accepts exactly the stage identities of that tag and no others, where the build and rebuild stages' identity is stage-sign.yml's (a Build or Rebuild record is accepted only under it, never under the former stage-build.yml or stage-reproducibility.yml identity).

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/policy/release-policy.template.json; bin/chain-verify.py; .github/policy/sigstore-trust.json*

> Status: - Round 7: `policy make` and `sign --check` take the committed trust file and the three PEMs next to the template as defaults (overridable by flags), with the same trust-hash check, so the first signed rc-tag run's and Release's pinned lines pass no file flags. PR 1 writes the template and the verify side only; Release signing the finished policy (rule 57) is PR 4. Witness's stage records cannot go to Rekor (Witness has no Rekor support); they carry the timestamp authority's stamp and are kept as release evidence (rule 53b). Decisions: - Step-8 round 1: - (a) the certificate chain is checked against the policy's root ONLY (the system trust store is switched off with -no-CAfile -no-CApath -no-CAstore -trusted), and tested with an attacker CA in SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR; - (b) timestamps come in two forms, a bare token in Witness records (go-witness timestamp/tsp.go) and a whole DER TimeStampResponse in a Sigstore bundle (protobuf-specs sigstore_common.proto), read by their type; - (c) Rekor is pinned to v1 by .github/policy/cosign-signing-config.json (cosign v3.1.3 `--signing-config`, an advisor-visible change to the pinned cosign command line: the default would use the TUF signing config, which may name Rekor v2 with no signed entry timestamp), and the log key in the trust file is the v1 key only; - (e) a record with a repeated JSON key or any signature count but one is refused. - Step-8 round 2 (NB-1, Opus): the certificate field of a record, and the verifier of a Rekor entry's body, must be EXACTLY ONE certificate PEM block with nothing but whitespace around it and no bytes after the certificate's outer SEQUENCE; the identity is read from that one DER and openssl verifies a PEM re-made from the same DER (before this, text or base64 before a genuine block was skipped by openssl but read as the identity by the homemade DER reader, so a self-made certificate with the right identity placed before any genuine certificate was accepted); every JSON reader is UTF-8 only (UTF-16/32 are refused, not guessed). - `sign --check` and `check-build-record` take exactly one of --template (the committed template: the per-tag policy is made there from GITHUB_REF) and --policy (a finished policy); the stage-sign.yml line and its pin changed from `--policy <template>` to `--template <template>`. - The flag `--rekor-stub` keeps its name only because later pull requests (PR 2-4) pin lines against it; it names the file of Rekor entries a bundle carries. - Opus N-9 is left as a documented note (no change). - Step-8 round 3 (B-1, both seats): the time of a timestamp is read ONLY from the bare token that the timestamp authority signed (a whole response is first required to have a clean status, no status string other than the TSA default ("unspecified") and no failure info, and is then reduced to its token with `openssl ts -reply -token_out`; the TSA's signature is verified over that same token), because a response's status section lies outside the TSA's signature and an edited statusString `x\nTime stamp: <date>` used to set the time compared with the certificate's validity; the stamp form is bound to the record type (a Witness collection carries the bare token `tsp`, the provenance the whole response `rfc3161-response`; the signed release policy either, PR 4 decides) and a mismatch is refused; a genTime with milliseconds is read and the fraction dropped; a certificate with a repeated extension (a second SAN, a second Build Config URI) is refused; the DER reader is not a general parser and trusts only the structure of a Fulcio-signed certificate. - `actions` follows a listed local composite action wherever it is stored, including under .github/workflows/, and skips following only a reference that names a .yml/.yaml file (a reusable workflow, judged as a workflow of its own). - The token of the key and token attempts must name exactly <repo>/.github/workflows/stage-sign.yml@<ref> of this repository (GITHUB_REPOSITORY). - Codex security round 1 (Oct 10): - (S1) after cosign, `sign` refuses a bundle with no or an empty timestamp list or Rekor entry list, naming each, verifies the two files it wrote as stage sign and requires the payload cosign signed to be, as parsed JSON with exact types (true is not 1, 1 is not 1.0), the statement Sign built (Opus round-1 verify F1, H2) before it prints ok; --out must not exist yet (., a folder, a file or a symlink is a usage error before anything runs) and any refusal, or any failure of that self-check, removes only the files Sign wrote and the folder it made (H1); - (S2) a Rekor entries file whose `entries` is not a list of objects is a refusal, never a traceback; - (S3) base64 must be canonical (re-encoding gives the same text) and JSON readers refuse NaN, Infinity, -Infinity and numbers that overflow to infinity (1e400); - (S4) only `actions` imports PyYAML; the Sign path runs on the standard library. - Codex security round 3 (Oct 10): an envelope field of the wrong JSON type is a refusal, and the issuer (.1.8) and Build Config URI (.1.18) extensions must each be one DER UTF8String TLV (Fulcio's v2 OID specification). - Codex security round 2 (Oct 10): every certificate of the Fulcio chain and of the TSA chain is checked AT the stamp's authenticated genTime (openssl -attime at the whole second below it, never -no_check_time), so an intermediate or a TSA signer that had expired, or was not yet valid, then is refused; genTime keeps its fraction (12:00:00.5 is after a certificate ending 12:00:00; for the certificate window openssl's check at the whole second below already decides, the fraction decides the 10-minute allowance after the verification clock, and a case pins that); a Rekor entry's logIndex and integratedTime must be canonical decimal strings, which fits the protobuf-JSON Sigstore bundle (int64 as strings): the Rekor REST API writes these fields as JSON numbers, which are refused, so the later pull request that produces the --rekor-stub file must take the entries from the bundle or emit protobuf-JSON strings; `sign` with no cosign on PATH is a refusal that removes the output folder it made. - Advisor reading, Oct 9 (handoff 0334; the ratified text is unchanged): a stage's identity in rules 52/52a/57 is the certificate whose SAN (Build Signer URI) is the stage file at the tag AND whose Build Config URI extension (OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.18, the top-level workflow) is release.yml at the same tag, issued by GitHub's OIDC issuer; the policy pins all three. - Witness's own verify can check the issuer but not the Build Config URI (in-toto-witness options/verify.go:80-99), so bin/chain-verify.py checks it. Stated exclusions: - (d) the Rekor entry in the tests is SYNTHETIC but has the real fields (sigstore-go pkg/tlog/entry.go, protobuf-specs sigstore_rekor.proto, Rekor dsse 0.0.1); the first signed rc-tag run captures a genuine bundle to replace it, and confirms the cosign bundle shape and whether the issuer extension is .1.8 or .1.1; Open items: - OPEN until one genuine cosign v3.1.3 bundle is captured at the first signed rc-tag run (cutover checklist): the verifier requires a Rekor v1 inclusionPromise (signed entry timestamp); a proof-only entry (inclusion proof without a promise) would be refused. - The OIDC issuer is read from OID .1.8; the spike certificate dumps list .1.1 and not .1.8, so the first signed rc-tag run must confirm .1.8 is present on a real certificate.

### REQ-CHAIN-003 — Each stage verifies the one before it; only standard record types; every action pinned

Every stage after Build shall first verify the previous stage's record, as Sign signed it, with one shared plain script and stop on failure, naming the stage; a record whose only signature is the building job's throwaway key, and any *.local.json, is refused by every verifier; only Witness's standard records, SLSA provenance and the signed release policy shall exist as signed record types; every signed record shall have a distinct claim and a named consumer (the record types under Sign's identity are three: the release provenance, Build's collection and Rebuild's collection, told apart by predicate type and collection name); and every action reference shall be a full commit digest and be on the committed allowed-actions list.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: bin/chain-verify.py; .github/policy/allowed-actions.json; .github/policy/chain-records.json; .github/policy/chain-scripts.json; check-action-pins.py*

The hash lists are tripwires: a listed file changes only with a visible hash edit in the same pull request; a script edited together with its row in chain-scripts.json is caught only by review and the pinned judge, because the judge reads that JSON from the pull request's own tree. They are in the pull request's own control; an independent control would need CODEOWNERS or ruleset entries on .github/policy/** and bin/chain-*-test.sh, an owner permission change not made here. - Closed lists (.github/policy/): id-token-jobs.json, the jobs that may hold id-token: write, a reason each (any other holder, matched case-insensitively, a stale entry, or an unparsable workflow fails; a merge key, `<<` or `!!merge`, at any depth of any workflow or composite action is refused, and one that does not parse as a single YAML document is a finding; composite actions are found anywhere in the repository, any case); legacy-stage-files.json, the eleven legacy stage files PRs 2-4 rewrite, pinned by sha256 (the wiring and records judges leave out their own findings but follow the LISTED scripts they run and what they produce; an UNLISTED file they run is never scanned; a changed one is judged in full; the list goes with the last of them); build-config-files.json, the build configuration outside bin/ and .github/ pinned by sha256, with .goreleaser.yaml held to a closed key set, its two hooks, and each build (no repeated id) with env, flags and ldflags exactly as today; chain-signers.json, every non-provenance signing call with a reason; chain-scripts.json, the scripts a stage may run by sha256 (only bin/chain-verify.py may sign provenance). - The id-token list is per job: it closes unlisted jobs, including remote reusable workflows, in-process libraries, files outside bin/ and .github/, and tools missing from the signer table. A signer step added to a listed job is seen when the shared signer table names it (@actions/attest is in it); otherwise review and the pin checker see it. - Python puts a script's directory first on sys.path, so a file in bin/ named after a standard-library module would replace that module inside the Sign job, whose SAN really is stage-sign.yml (the SAN pin cannot see it). Closed structurally: the Sign step runs `python3 -I -B` and every python3 line of a stage file runs with -I; chain-verify.py compiles its two helper modules from their bytes after checking each against its sha256 in chain-scripts.json (no bytecode cache is consulted; tests prove a bin/fractions.py and an unchecked-hash __pycache__ copy are not run, and changed helper bytes are refused). The judge refuses any file or directory under bin/ or .github/ named after a standard-library module, and any __pycache__ directory or .pyc/.pyo/.so/.pyd/.dll file there (names matched case-insensitively). The -I rule covers stage-file lines only; a third-party name (bin/yaml.py) on a job without -I is backed by the file allowlist for bin/ and Release's SAN pin. Release's own `policy make` in stage-promote.yml runs with -I too. - Information, not a gap in Release: an unlisted file run by a frozen id-token job (bin/vex-forms.py, bin/patch-decide.py and the like) is not scanned by these suites; keyed signing is outside the keyless model (the only signing-like secret, AUDITOR_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, mints App tokens); neither can pass Release's SAN pin. Obfuscated signers are out of scope (owner, Oct 3); `docker buildx --attest type=provenance` writes unsigned provenance. Decisions: - AC3: no known-red allowance; the real tree is an ordinary `expect ok` with the frozen files' own findings left out. - AC4 is narrow on purpose: `actions` rejects today's release.yml, stage-build.yml and stage-promote.yml until PRs 2-4 rewrite them; it refuses repeated keys (trimmed, case-folded) and malformed shapes by name. The pin checker's repeated-key rule is its own pull request (pin-check-repeated-keys). - AC5 (narrowed, advisor 0334): only release.yml calls stage-sign.yml and no stage file calls another; scan.yml and main-candidate-rescan.yml stay allowed callers because the policy pins the Build Config URI. - `stage-start` starts only from rebuild<-build, check<-build, sign<-build and release<-{build, sign, rebuild, check}, with Sign's digest-format and subject-type checks. - CI: the four suites are steps of ci.yml's allowlist job, judging a copy of the tracked files; a lint case refuses any pipe into a quiet grep under pipefail. Stated exclusions: - A command built at run time inside a listed script; a signer reached only through an argv array or a program another program spawns; an unlisted file run by a frozen id-token job (backed by Release's SAN pin). A signer in a script outside chain-scripts.json run by a NON-stage listed job (bash bin/x.sh with cosign sign-blob, `go run .../cmd/cosign`, `gh attestation sign`, `npx @sigstore/cli`, rekor-cli) is not seen; it signs with that job's own OIDC identity, so the SAN is that workflow and Release's SAN pin (REQ-CHAIN-001-AC4) refuses it. Open items: - Cosign is Sign's tool (rule 53b needs a Rekor entry, which Witness cannot write).

### REQ-CHAIN-004 — Build runs sealed, under Witness, after admission, and hands Sign only a digest list

The Build stage shall be one workflow file and one identity holding two jobs, an apk matrix job (one runner per native architecture) and one assemble job, each directly on a GitHub-hosted VM and never in a container, in which Witness is installed first (pinned by checksum) and everything else runs as one committed script under Witness; that script first admits the tagged commit with every check the old admission stage made, then builds the package and the images with the cache lane's two scripts inside a network-less namespace, checks the built server reports its real version, and writes digests.json, the only thing Sign accepts; Witness records each Build step inside the Build job with a throwaway key that the job generates and discards, so that signature carries no trust and no verifier accepts it; the Sign stage checks the record's product digests against the artifacts it receives and signs the record keyless under its own identity with the Sigstore timestamp; the record never contains the job's identity-token variables; Build holds no secret, no registry credential and no identity token.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/stage-build.yml; bin/build-stage-apk.sh; bin/build-stage-assemble.sh; bin/build-admit.py; bin/build-version-check.py*

THIS RULE REFUSES HONEST CONFUSION EARLY, with a clear message; it is not the security boundary. Hardening note only: the callers judge reads YAML with a loader that keeps the last of two equal keys; a duplicate-key-refusing loader would close that, and is not changed here. With v0.3.0 at HEAD the single line git tag --force v0.0.0-rc.1 HEAD still leaves the Go stamp v0.3.0 (the test's control); the delete, make and check lines give the stamp v0.0.0-rc.1 with vcs.revision equal to HEAD, leave the remote untouched and are idempotent. The test skips cleanly, still counted, when go or git is missing; the CI runner has both. artifact-acceptance (AC14, step-6 round 3, F3): the value SHAPE of expected-checksums changes, from the raw checksums.txt text to the one-line digests JSON, and the artifact it reads is Build's dist (the four Linux archives) instead of dist-snapshot. The guard is tested with real git (unset, empty, false, FALSE, TRUE, 1 and 'true ' all refuse and leave every tag) and its position before the first git tag is asserted in the wiring test. ### REQ-CHAIN-005 — Rebuild repeats the build on a fresh machine and blocks on any difference

The Rebuild stage shall be one workflow file and one identity (an apk job on each native architecture, rapk on ubuntu-24.04 and rapk-arm on ubuntu-24.04-arm, and an assemble job that needs both) on fresh GitHub-hosted VMs that first verifies Build's record as Sign signed it, then builds the same commit with the same pinned tools, the same two scripts and the same build date, compares every digest with Build's record, and records only a verdict naming each differing item (the Rebuild job's Witness record is made under a throwaway key and trusted by nobody; the second job of the Sign stage signs it keyless), and runs alongside Check after Sign, needing Build and Sign.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/stage-reproducibility.yml; bin/build-stage-rebuild-apk.sh; bin/build-stage-rebuild-assemble.sh; bin/chain-verify.py; .github/workflows/release.yml*

> Release publishes Build's bytes and never Rebuild's (rule 64), so Rebuild's only output is its verdict. The compared items follow cache's interface note: per-architecture apk (apk-tool.py digest), local index, modules SBOM, inputs manifest, full lock file, the OCI image index digest and each per-architecture manifest digest (OUT/<variant>.digest and .manifests), the SBOM files and the binary; the layout of the apkindex, inputs manifest and binary items is PROPOSED/UNVERIFIED in the tests. Snapshot Rebuild (AC7; advisor validation of the snapshot step 5, Oct 9): the PR gate's reproducibility check keeps its two independent assemblies in snapshot form; the snapshot Rebuild has no signature to verify (a snapshot record is refused by verify and stage-start), so its trust in Build's items.json is the hash the snapshot-build record holds for it, checked by rebuild-compare --snapshot inside the same workflow run.
