### REQ-AUD-018 — The auditor layout and coverage gate; its second review is enforced outside the repository

The auditor shall keep everything auditor-related in the auditor directory, hold its Python to the same 100% coverage gate as the Go (except the listed exclusions), and let no change to the auditor merge without the independent second review, which the private review tooling enforces before merge; this repository judges no review record.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: auditor directory bin/auditor-layout-check.py; auditor directory tests/coverage-gate.sh; .github/workflows/agent-review-gate.yml; .github/workflows/ci.yml*

> The `then` text of AC1, AC2 and AC3 is a PARAPHRASE of the ratified sentences with the literal auditor path replaced by 'the auditor directory' (the layout check forbids that literal in this file); the VERBATIM ratified sentences are quoted in the comments above the three entries in test-evidence/mappings.yaml, which is exempt from the layout check. The second review that AC3 requires is enforced outside this repository, by the private review tooling, before merge. The trusted verdict auditor-review-gate (agent-review-gate.yml, always the default branch's copy) runs main's action-pin checker, allowlist guard, pin-wiring judge and scanner guard over the pull request head, read as git objects; it judges no review record and reads no substitute. That the main branch ruleset REQUIRES the checks is not checkable from the repository and is an inspection item for the owner's settings. AC1 exemptions in the layout check beyond the AC text: .github/dependabot.yml and .githooks/pre-commit (read as allowlist entries), plus mappings.yaml and unmapped.yaml (owner, Oct 2) and bin/patch-decide.py with its test (owner, Oct 3). The coverage gate's exclusion list (coverage-exclusions.txt in the auditor directory) is not in the AC2 text, so "100% coverage" is read as zero uncovered eligible statements. Gate-workflow digest (the scanner guard, cache PR #316): the pin checker (bin/check-action-pins.py in the auditor directory) pins the gate workflow by GATE_WORKFLOW_SHA256, a frozen set of exactly one digest, 699abb31 (the gate workflow of #316), taken by its gate_digest (action pins masked). The bootstrap digest adcfd54f (the gate workflow on main before #316) was removed in the release-candidate review (rc-5b B1), so a revert of the gate workflow to it is refused. A different digest fails with a message naming the accepted one.

### REQ-AUD-019 — The auditor unit tests touch no real system path

The auditor's Python unit tests shall not open, list, create, link, stat or resolve any real system path: a runtime guard armed for the whole test run fails any such call that leaves the test's temporary directory, the repository checkout and the interpreter's own environment; the Python tests are also scanned statically in full for a system-path literal outside a reviewed allow-list; and every other test script (shell) is scanned statically only for a symbolic link made to an absolute target and for creating files without a temporary directory. Go and Java tests are not scanned statically; the runtime guard covers whatever test discovery actually runs.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: auditor directory bin/tests/fs_guard.py; auditor directory bin/tests/test_fs_guard.py; auditor directory bin/tests/system_path_allowlist.py*

> The runtime guard is an audit hook plus wrappers installed by test_0000_arm_fs_guard.py, the first module discovery imports (digits sort before letters; test_fs_guard.py asserts that it sorts first and that an early and a late module are both guarded). Import-time code of a module that sorted before it would be unguarded; none does, and a new one named test_0* before it would fail that assertion; it judges the resolved path of each call (symbolic links followed, ".." applied after a link, a dir_fd or an open fd resolved to its directory) against the temporary directory, the checkout and the interpreter environment (read only), and is proven by mutants run in a container. The static literal scan keeps a reviewed allow-list (system_path_allowlist.py) whose whole-file rows pin the file byte for byte. The shell scan is limited to ln -s / cp -s (and the hard-link form) with an absolute target and to a script that creates files without ever calling mktemp or tempfile (the mktemp rule); the scan does not check that every file lands under the temp directory, the runtime guard (AC1) is what catches a stray path. The shell checks are a lint of plain forms, not a security control. The static scans read only git-tracked files and skip test_fs_guard.py itself and the coverage gate script; Python helpers outside the test file name pattern (fixtures, fs_guard.py) are not literal-scanned; a metadata exemption listed in AC1 (ancestors of a root, sysconfig directories, the stdlib zip, pyvenv.cfg, the trusted user base, /dev/null and /dev/urandom, descriptors open at arming, ctypes.CDLL(None)) is deliberate, not a gap. A container job whose HOME is not the account's home directory loses the user-scheme metadata entries (coverage stats them); the guard then refuses, it does not widen. The runtime guard is a tripwire for accidental access to real system paths by the repository's own tests; it is not a security boundary against test code that deliberately subverts it (replacing the SQLite authorizer, swallowing the refusal, or altering sys.path). Documented residuals of the runtime guard (it is a tripwire, see AC1): a test can replace the SQLite authorizer with set_authorizer; a refusal can be swallowed by an except Exception that catches the SQLite DatabaseError, or by asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True) in the main thread; a C library that opens a file without emitting an audit event (ssl, posix.stat) is not seen; other runners than discovery (python -m unittest <module>, the direct test_panel_sdk_probe.py run in ci.yml, pytest) do not arm the guard; and a package that sorts before the arming module would be imported unguarded. PLAIN FORMS ONLY (AC2): the Python literal scan detects an absolute path whose first component is one of a fixed name list (etc usr var private Library System opt bin sbin dev home root proc sys Users tmp Applications Volumes run srv lib lib64 boot mnt nix cores Network snap workspace github media data afs net scratch export exports nfs Developer lost+found vol pkg swapfile imagegeneration datadisk cdrom lib32 libx32 init __w _work docker-entrypoint.d entrypoint.sh sw firmlinks and the *.usr-is-merged names), in any letter case, with extra slashes, /./ or /../ before the name, a digit or underscore after it, a brace list (/{etc,usr}) or a one-character ? wildcard (/e?c); a first component that starts with a dot or contains a glob character; ~user; a chain of two or more ../; --option=/abs, an attached -C/, source=/, a redirect into /; the bare root (/, //, /., /.., /./, quoted, with an r/b/u/f prefix, or as an argument of a listed command such as ls, cd, find, grep, cat, cp, tar, git, test), cwd='/', open('/'), os.path.join('/', ...); os.sep and os.path.sep as a call argument, an assignment or inside abspath, realpath and normpath (not as a string-method argument such as .split(os.sep)); a home form (~/, $HOME, ${HOME, expanduser, Path.home, os.environ['HOME'], os.getenv('HOME'), os.environ.get('HOME'), pwd.getpwuid, pwd.getpwnam, cd ~, a bare cd, file: URIs, a chain of three ../); and, by syntax tree, os.symlink, os.link, symlink_to and hardlink_to with an absolute constant in any argument. It does not detect a path built at run time or by concatenation, a first component outside the list (unless it starts with a dot or contains a glob character), or anything in a file outside the name pattern. The shell checks (AC3) detect: ln or cp (also by /bin/ln or /usr/bin/ln) with the flags -s, -l, --symbolic, --symbolic-link in any position, or a hard ln, whose operand is absolute: starts with / (also / alone and //), ~, $'/..', a {/x,y} brace list, a ${V:-/x} ${V-/x} ${V=/x} ${V+/x} ${V:=/x} ${V:+/x} default (the ${V?/x} and ${V:?/x} forms are not detected), or an attached -t/x or --target-directory=/x, across a backslash-newline continuation; and a script in which a creator command word (mkdir, touch, cp, mv, ln, install, tee, mkfifo, mknod, dd of=, sed -i, git init or clone, after VAR=, sudo, env, command, exec, time, nice, xargs, !, then, do) or a redirect (>, >>, >| to a word that is not a descriptor &N, &-, a process substitution or /dev/null) appears outside comments, single and double quotes (except their $( ) and backtick substitutions), $(( )) and heredoc bodies, and mktemp is never a command word and python tempfile is never called outside a comment. Recorded residuals of the last verification passes (not fixed, by the advisor's hard stop): os.listdir('/dev/null') (or of /dev/urandom) reaches the operating system's NotADirectoryError, so "nothing else may be done to the devices" is not strictly enforced for listing a device (it does no harm: neither device is a directory); a spelling variant of the heredoc opener such as `echo \" "<<EOF"` (an escaped quote before a quoted opener) is not recognised as quoted, so a creator after it can be missed; and one comment in the shell lexer (the arithmetic blanking) was stale after the let change and has been corrected as a comment-only line. Go and Java tests are out of the static scan by decision; they run under the same guard only where discovery runs them in the Python interpreter.

when a call opens, lists, creates, links, renames, removes, stats or resolves a path (including through a symbolic link, a dir_fd, an open file descriptor, a socket address or a database file) that is outside the test's temporary directory, the repository checkout and the interpreter's own environment, or writes inside the interpreter's environment other than its bytecode cache; ## SBOM

### REQ-SBOM-001 — The Go module list is written by the build from the binary's own embedded list

The Go module list, which neither melange nor apko writes, shall be written by a build step from the vendored module list and the binary's own embedded module list, and signed with the release; no scanner makes or gates the SBOM. The SBOM lists the modules the binary embeds; every embedded path and version must be in both vendor/modules.txt and dependency-provenance.json (a subset, not equality); modules that are vendored but not built are in the dependency list, not the SBOM.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: bin/go-module-sbom.py*

> Advisor reading, binding: path and version are compared; the vendor-mode binary list carries no hashes. Wiring the tool into the apk build (bin/build-apk.sh) and signing the file with the release belong to the melange pull request, not this one.

## BUILDTOOLS

### REQ-BUILDTOOLS-001 — The build's helper tools check apks, recipes, locks and image layouts without the network

The helper tools the v0.3.0 build calls shall inspect and verify its inputs and outputs offline and fail closed: bin/apk-tool.py (apk sections, signer, binary and inputs manifest), bin/gen-recipes.py (both melange recipes are generated from one reviewed, pinned template and differ only in the package name, the description and the two FIPS lines), bin/install-build-tools.sh (melange and apko by pinned checksum), bin/go-module-sbom.py (the module list of the binary) and bin/apko-lock.sh (base lock versus full lock, archive verification, evidence list). The image digest tool and the sealed-namespace probe are in REQ-BUILDTOOLS-002.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: bin/apk-tool.py; bin/gen-recipes.py; build/melange.yaml.tmpl; bin/install-build-tools.sh; bin/apko-lock.sh; bin/go-module-sbom.py*

> Each tool's argv and exit codes are in its header comment (the pipeline lane reads them). The drivers that call them (bin/build-apk.sh, bin/assemble-image.sh) belong to the melange and apko pull requests. melange 0.61.2 and apko 1.4.6 (both public for more than 7 days when pinned) are pinned by the sha256 values in the release checksums.txt files fetched over HTTPS from the projects' GitHub releases. Known residuals: bin/apk-tool.py refuses a PAX extended header as the FIRST header of stream 0 (the signature stream must start with a plain header); elsewhere only the exact key APK-TOOLS.checksum.SHA1 is accepted. A forwarded-value echo in error messages is not escaped. The real melange and apko runs are pending the runner proof. Review-round-9 ruling: the generator closes the placeholders, the substitutions, the step conditions and the places of the name and description, and pins the template by sha256; it does NOT judge the shell in the template (that is the human and reviewer checklist at the top of build/melange.yaml.tmpl); the final control for the FIPS binary is build-apk.sh's check of the packaged binary. The proof greps only the GOFIPS140 stamp (a go.mod godebug fips140=off would show in DefaultGODEBUG, which is not checked) and writes to the fixed path /tmp/fscache-gobuildinfo.txt inside the melange sandbox. The apk is read whole into memory. The header walk is the check; the tar reader is used only after the walk agrees with it on the number of entries. Data files (review round 9): the package pins of the build environment come from build/locks/melange.lock and the certified Go Cryptographic Module from build/locks/fips-module.txt, each with a closed line grammar; the generator holds no FIPS constant, so the daily refresh and the FIPS-module check change only those files and the generated recipes stay equal to the generator's output.

## CHAIN

### REQ-CHAIN-006 — Check judges the candidates and signs what it found

The Check stage shall run, in one stage file beside Rebuild and off Build's output (the job check, and the job check-arm64 for the linux/arm64 artifact checks), every scanner the policy lists, the Gradle and Maven acceptance suites, the no-phone-home test, the FIPS start check and every customer-guide command against the exact candidate digests, as plain scripts that know nothing about signing, under Witness in three plainly named steps (scanners, acceptance, runtime) each limited to 9 minutes by the one shared helper, and sign its results as one Witness record per step under its own identity; it shall hold no registry or key access, and any failure shall stop the release and name Check.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/stage-verify.yml; .github/workflows/release.yml; .github/workflows/acceptance.yml; bin/witnessed.sh; bin/check-stage.sh; bin/check-scan.sh; bin/check-fips.sh; bin/check-acceptance.sh; bin/check-guide.sh; bin/acceptance-gradle.sh; bin/acceptance-gradle-capped.sh; bin/acceptance-maven.sh; bin/acceptance-maven-capped.sh; bin/acceptance-egress.sh; bin/acceptance-k8s.sh; bin/acceptance-serve.sh; .github/policy/scanners.json*

AC15 (advisor, Oct 10, option 1: fresh databases at scan time from the scanners' own hosts only): grype's database status is read from the shape recorded in the scanner fixtures of the auditor directory (fixtures/scanners)/grype.json (descriptor.db.status: from, built, valid; host grype.anchore.io, digest the sha256 in the download URL's checksum). osv-scanner (advisor, Oct 10, from osv-scanner v2.6.0 docs/offline-mode.md) runs in offline mode with --download-offline-databases into an empty OSV_SCANNER_LOCAL_DB_CACHE_DIRECTORY; the evidence is read from the downloaded <ecosystem>/all.zip files: source https://osv-vulnerabilities.storage.googleapis.com/ <ecosystem>/all.zip (the only allowed osv host), digest the zip's sha256, date the newest record `modified`, recorded as db_newest_record_modified: for osv-scanner the date recorded is the newest record `modified` in the downloaded database, not a database build date (grype's db_built_or_published is its database build time). db_source_basis is "observed" for grype (its status output names the URL) and "documented" for osv-scanner: neither its files nor its output name the URL it downloaded from, so a wrong osv host can only be caught on GitHub (a network allow-list on the runner, or osv-scanner's log) and is listed under proof on GitHub. The osv cache directory is empty before the osv runs of this job (made fresh, or, when OSV_SCANNER_LOCAL_DB_CACHE_DIRECTORY is already set, refused unless empty), so every database is downloaded in this job. RULE 68, AS AMENDED BY THE OWNER (Oct 9, 16:47 EDT; harness spike (d): Witness checks the Fulcio certificate at the TIMESTAMP's time, so a command that runs past the certificate's ten minutes yields a record that never verifies): every witnessed command is limited to 9 minutes. The cap lives in ONE place, the helper bin/witnessed.sh, which PR 2 defines; the helper judge in bin/chain-check-shape.py is kept identical to PR 2's seam and is deleted in favour of it once PR 2 lands. Check is split into three steps so that none nears the cap; real phase times for Build are in the PR 2 notes. The owner also asked that the code not be ugly or overly complex to pass the rule: the stage file is four short lines, reviewers get readability for a human as an explicit brief item, and a judge that needs cleverness is simplified. CUTOVER RULE (advisor 0341): PR 3 merges into the integration branch chain-v030 only; the old chain (stage-verify.yml and the acceptance stages as they are today) stays live on main until the one cutover pull request. The real-tree cases of the tests are red until the implementation PR. Existing ACs this must not weaken: REQ-REL-004-AC1 (every scanner reports its package count; zero packages fail) and the REQ-SCAN and REQ-FIPS requirements. The scanner list is .github/policy/scanners.json (today grype and osv-scanner); the daily rescan's other scanners (Inspector, Scout, Google, Snyk) are not part of Check. The images reach Check as files (OCI tarballs from Build's artifacts), not from a registry: Check logs in to no registry and holds no packages permission. Anything in the scripts' command lines that no existing file fixes is PROPOSED/UNVERIFIED in the test headers: the guide file name (the www lane's customer guide, docs/verify-release.md), the acceptance suites' wrapper command lines, and the results file names. CREDENTIALS (coordinator correction, Oct 9): Check needs no cloud scanner federation. The release scanners in scanners.json are grype and osv-scanner, which need no credential; the AWS Inspector and GCP trusts serve only scan.yml and main-candidate-rescan.yml. The SNYK_TOKEN that today's stage-verify.yml takes as a secret is not needed by the listed scanners (scanners.json: Snyk runs in the daily rescan only), so Check holds no secret at all (decided from scanners.json; if the owner adds a scanner that needs a credential, that is a changed rule and a new read-back). id-token: write exists only so Witness can sign Check's own record. WORDING BROUGHT TO THE CODE (Oct 24; the text above is history): Check's four steps run under bin/witnessed-local.sh (owner Oct 22, ops/docs/ratify/2026-10-22-witness-signed-outside-build.md), signed with a throwaway key, no identity token and no Sigstore timestamp in the Check jobs; Sign re-signs the records keyless. The Check jobs hold contents read only. AC1, AC4, AC9 and AC11 describe that.

### REQ-CHAIN-007 — Release verifies everything first, then alone holds the credentials and publishes the exact bytes

The Release stage shall verify every earlier stage's signed record, in a fixed order, first in a job that holds neither a secret nor a write token and again in the credential-holding job before any step of it explicitly binds a credential, and only then use the apk signing key and the registry credentials, which no other job holds, to sign the released apks, publish by digest the exact bytes Build made and Rebuild and Check judged, read the registry back, sign everything a customer verifies keyless with a Rekor entry (images in both registries, SBOMs, lock files, the dependency evidence and the release policy), and attach the evidence to the release, without building anything and without creating a version tag.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: .github/workflows/stage-promote.yml; .github/workflows/release.yml; bin/release-verify.sh; bin/release-apks.sh; bin/release-publish.sh; bin/release-sign.sh; bin/release-assets.sh; .github/policy/chain-scripts.json*

> ADVISOR RULINGS (Oct 9, on the read-back). (a) A release candidate verifies exactly like a final release, so the tag rule is vX.Y.Z and vX.Y.Z-rcN and nothing else (the dotted spelling -rc.N of this ruling was dropped by the accepted grammar of Oct 12); PR 1's policy make --tag must accept the same two shapes (its tests and code are on the PR 1 branch and need the same widening). (b) The release policy is signed with cosign, keyless, under Release's identity, so it has a Rekor entry a customer can check; Witness records stay extra evidence. (c) Signatures are made in both registries. (d) SUPERSEDED Oct 12 by the accepted AC5/AC6 text: the proof of the whole chain (REQ-CHAIN-001-AC5) is the signed rc-tag run cut on main after the cutover merge, recorded by the marker of REQ-CHAIN-001-AC6; it is not a dry run before the merge. CUTOVER RULE (advisor 0341): PR 4 merges into the integration branch chain-v030 only; the live chain on main is untouched until the one cutover pull request, which has its own read-back, a final whole-diff review round and names the switch moment. A v* tag is the owner's; the first real run is the owner's rc tag. Release creates no tag. THE WITNESS WRAPPING is the one seam shared with PR 2 and 3 (owner's rule 68 amendment, Oct 9, and the readability request): every Witness step runs through the single helper bin/witnessed.sh STEP SCRIPT with timeout -k 20 540 inside it; the stage file never repeats Witness flags. Release has six such steps (release-verify, release-apks, release-publish, release-sign, release-assets, release-postverify) so that a credential reaches only the step that needs it and a step stays far below the ten-minute Fulcio certificate. PROPOSED/UNVERIFIED: the script names and command lines of bin/release-*.sh; the tool that re-signs an apk with the stored key (melange sign is assumed; cache-3f's apk-tool.py signer reports assembly.rsa.pub, release.rsa.pub or unsigned and is fixed by cache's tests); the copy tool (crane, pinned by checksum through bin/install-scanner.sh); the registry-state check before publishing; the artifact names images and apks; the floating tags (REQ-REL-009 moves them for finals only); and that cosign's bundle for a sign-blob holds a Rekor entry (tlogEntries) in the shape PR 1 verifies; that PR 1's stage-start accepts --rekor-stub for Sign's provenance (else one more verify line); the crane entry of bin/install-scanner.sh (version, asset names, CRANE_BASE_URL; tested by bin/chain-install-crane-test.sh). The environment named release restricted to v* tags is the owner's setting (note only, no test). This PR cannot be run end to end before PRs 1 to 3 exist.

## BUILDTOOLS

### REQ-BUILDTOOLS-002 — The image digest is the OCI index digest and a sealed namespace is checked by a probe

The image digest shall be the digest of the OCI index of the image tar (bin/oci-digest.py reads both the standard OCI layout and the tar real apko writes), and bin/net-probe.py shall tell a sealed network namespace from a leaky one by the errno of a connect attempt.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: bin/oci-digest.py; bin/net-probe.py*

> Real apko v1.4.6 writes a tar with no oci-layout, blobs named sha256:<hex> and index.json as the multi-architecture index; its digest is the sha256 of index.json. Known residuals: the real apko run, the bubblewrap runner and the kernel seal are pending the runner proof (no privileged container is run on the owner's Mac).

| REQ-BUILDTOOLS-002-AC2 | Given a network namespace; when net-probe.py runs; then it connects to 192.0.2.1:9 and exits with the connect errno, so 101 (ENETUNREACH) means the namespace has no route (rule 40) | unit |  | approved | 1 item(s) |

## VEND

### REQ-VEND-001 — Vendored dependencies with checked provenance

The release source shall include vendor/ generated in CI from checksum-verified downloads; every Go build shall use only vendored code; dependency-provenance.json at the repository root shall list per module its path, version, hash, checksum-log entry, upstream origin, commit (pseudo-versions) or tag (tagged versions), and license; any module whose origin or checksum-log entry cannot be found shall fail the build.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: bin/vendor-provenance.py; bin/vendor-provenance-records.py; bin/vendor-check.sh; bin/vendoring-test.sh; bin/vendor-provenance-test.sh; .github/workflows/ci.yml; bin/check-file-allowlist.sh; vendor/modules.txt; dependency-provenance.json; .github/workflows/dependabot-reviewer.yml*

> Landed in two parts: the regenerate-and-compare check, the required `vendor` job and the vendor/ allowlist pattern (AC2, AC3, AC11 for bin/vendor-check.sh) in the vendor-check PR; the vendored tree, the provenance file and its check, the evidence file and the public wording (AC1, AC4-AC10, AC12-AC14, the provenance step of AC3 and AC11 for bin/vendor-provenance.py) in the vendored-tree PR, whose tests are bin/vendor-provenance-test.sh; the vendor-check cases stay in bin/vendoring-test.sh. The vendor job runs the provenance check; the release stage that assembles the evidence file is a separate release-chain change. AC13's public text (docs/dependencies.md) is a DRAFT held for the owner's discussion. build reads the sumdb record, the origins and the reviewed licenses file as files, so the network fetch of those records is a separate CI step outside this requirement. The SPDX licence id comes from a committed, reviewed licenses file, never from detection.

## BUILDAPK

### REQ-BUILDAPK-001 — The apk is built by melange from vendored source, sealed from the network, assembly-signed

The fscache apk, regular and FIPS, shall be built by melange from two recipe files of identical source that differ only in the FIPS setting, from vendored Go code, the Go toolchain from the archive and build tools pinned by version, with the network cut at the kernel; it shall be signed during Build and Rebuild with a committed non-secret assembly key, and signed with the release key only by the Release job after Build and Rebuild produce the same package contents.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: build/melange.yaml; build/melange-fips.yaml; bin/build-apk.sh; bin/release-sign-apks.sh; build/keys/assembly.rsa; build/keys/assembly.rsa.pub; build/keys/release.rsa.pub*

> Real-run evidence for this group is PENDING the runner proof; the seal (rules 38-41) is not counted as proven until then; the earlier Addenda A-C ran on an older commit of the scripts. Tested with stub melange, sudo and unshare; the real melange run, the bubblewrap runner and the kernel seal will be proven on the Linux runner (rule 41 sealed proof). build/keys/release.rsa.pub is a placeholder file: the PR that commits the real public half must change the placeholder test and the key-shape test. The three-step recipes (setup, build, record, stamp) generated from build/melange.yaml.tmpl have NOT been run with real melange yet: the runner proof is pending. build/locks/melange.lock holds the whole resolved build-tool closure (resolved against live Wolfi on 2026-10-09 by real apko) and the recipes pin the same list; the daily refresh job keeps both current. The Go stamp check needs the version tag v<version> at the source HEAD in the workspace; a real melange run with a tagged source (0.3.0-rc.1) produced fscache-0.3.0_rc1-r0.apk, so melange accepts the underscore pre-release version. Known residuals, listed for the reviewers and not hidden: (1) release signing stages each signed apk as a .new file next to the original and renames after; a crash between the cp and the rename leaves a stray .new that the next run refuses to overwrite (a window, not a wrong release); (2) the X_OK check of the tool directory is not tested; (3) a write through a symlinked PARENT of --out is not refused beyond the directory itself; (4) a value forwarded into an error message is echoed back unescaped (an echo class, no code path acts on it). The real melange runs are pending the runner proof. Ordinary-failure vs network-attempt classification relies on a narrow stderr match; Connection refused / No route to host / Operation not permitted are not classified as AC5 network attempts (Codex round 9 finding 3, accepted as residual by the advisor Oct 10: the wide pattern over-matches ordinary failures such as bwrap EPERM).

## REFRESH

### REQ-REFRESH-001 — Image inputs and the certified FIPS module are kept fresh by jobs that only open pull requests

Once a day a job shall re-make the image lock files and re-resolve melange's build tools against live Wolfi; if anything changed it archives the new packages by digest, updates the locks and opens a pull request, never pushing to main; otherwise it does nothing. This job is the only updater of image recipes, apk packages and lock files. If Wolfi's signing key changed the job stops, opens no pull request and flags it for a human. If an old upstream version disappears the job notes it and does not fail. New Wolfi packages get no waiting period; signature and checksum checks and archiving still apply. The job's pull requests go through all normal checks and the rebuild-from-archive test. In the same daily run it shall also read Go's own certified-module file and, when a newer Go Cryptographic Module is certified, open a pull request that moves the FIPS build to it. The archive's package index shall be kept as the original Wolfi-signed file, versioned by its sha256, verified against the archived key, and an existing file under a digest name must hash to that name or the run fails closed.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: bin/refresh-inputs.sh; build/host-tools.yaml; build/locks/host-tools.lock; .github/workflows/go-freshness.yml; .github/dependabot.yml*

> Real-run evidence for this group is PENDING the runner proof; the seal (rules 38-41) is not counted as proven until then; the earlier Addenda A-C ran on an older commit of the scripts. The job is the `refresh` job of the existing go-freshness.yml workflow (no new workflow file). It opens pull requests with the auditor App's token, like the go.mod bump job, so bin/go-freshness-wiring-test.sh lists it as a credential consumer; the token's reach (a refresh/ branch and a pull request) was checked against the repository rulesets and the agent environment's branch policy (ruleset 21172637 targets only the default branch). Rebuilding the archive index and the check that a new lock verifies against the archive (bin/apko-lock.sh) belong to the apko pull request. Known residuals: with an open refresh PR and the pointer ahead, the pointer is accepted if it hashes to its own name (direction and signature are checked only on the next reconcile run); a forwarded-value echo in error messages is not escaped. Round-8 residuals: the fips-module recipe is left modified if the push or the pull request creation fails (the PR run is a fresh checkout); in a state where the archive is BEHIND the record the superseded-pull-request sentence can name an unrelated closed refresh pull request (the sentence begins 'No open refresh pull request was found'); the pointer-ahead state trusts any self-hashing index file until the next reconcile replaces it. AC17 reading: while a refresh pull request waits, a damaged archived file stops the job, including a file named only by the COMMITTED locks (an old version an upgrade leaves behind); a MISSING apk is not downloaded again by that run (the waiting pull request's own run, and the first run after it merges, do that), and a package that only main's lock names and that live Wolfi no longer resolves is verified against the committed lock but cannot be downloaded again. AC17 floor for the committed melange.lock: its old versions (name=version, no checksums) are checked for integrity (every gzip stream inflates, the control section's datahash equals the data stream's sha256), not against a checksum; authenticity of those files rests on the apko locks and the signed index. AC22 plain pointer: a legacy plain pointer is checked to be a SIGNED index before any early exit (also when it equals the record). AC22 legacy state: a plain APKINDEX.tar.gz that is the recorded index and is a signed index, with no versioned index/APKINDEX-<sha256> file yet, is accepted and is kept under its own digest by the first run that changes the index. The daily job edits only DATA files (the locks, build/locks/fips-module.txt) and asks bin/gen-recipes.py what the recipes become; it never edits the recipe template or its pin.

## ARCHIVE

### REQ-ARCHIVE-001 — The archive is pushed, pulled and checked by digest, with no way around the pointer

The archive of apk packages, package indexes and the Wolfi key file shall be stored as one OCI artifact in GHCR under a digest, by one script that only the refresh job calls (the only writer). Build, Rebuild and the refresh job shall pull it by exactly the digest committed in build/archive.json, before and outside the sealed build, into a staging directory, and refuse any digest or any file hash that differs from the pointer; no fallback to the live internet.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: bin/archive-push.sh; bin/archive-pull.sh; bin/archive-verify.py; build/archive.json*

> Every AC of this requirement is new English (AC9 is the tool-path convention, the same form as REQ-BUILDAPK-001-AC3). Not in this change: the refresh job's workflow edit, the real archive contents (the first refresh run creates them), registry deletion and retention, and any crane install beyond the version pinned in stage-promote.yml (the fixed path of crane is /usr/local/bin/crane, a TEST-SUBST line). Symlinks are refused by the push and by verify, and the refresh layout does not use one (advisor 0425, amended REQ-REFRESH-001-AC13): <arch>/APKINDEX.tar.gz is a regular-file COPY of index/APKINDEX-<sha256>.tar.gz, so the same sha256 is listed in the pointer under both names (archive-test covers a directory holding both). The refresh job writes build/archive.json from archive-push.sh's printed digest plus the sorted file list, with no new script. Crane (advisor 0425): installed at /usr/local/bin/crane with stage-promote.yml's exact pin (go install github.com/google/go-containerregistry/cmd/crane@v0.22.1); no workflow edit in this change. The version annotation of a layer is parsed from an apk file name (<name>-<version>-r<N>.apk) and is empty for other files.

## IMAGE

### REQ-IMAGE-001 — The image is assembled by apko from the archive alone, sealed from the network and proved so

The production and FIPS images shall be assembled by apko in one offline run for both architectures from the archive and our fresh apk only, with a committed base lock, a per-build full lock that must equal the base lock plus our apks (the program and fscache-baselayout), the network cut at the kernel, and an image digest that is the OCI index digest; the sealing and the lock method shall be proved by scripts that must be able to fail.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence implementation-only · source: build/apko.yaml; build/apko-fips.yaml; build/locks/apko.base.lock.json; build/locks/apko-fips.base.lock.json; bin/assemble-image.sh; bin/lock-proof.sh; bin/sealed-proof.sh*

> Real-run evidence for this group is PENDING the runner proof; the seal (rules 38-41) is not counted as proven until then; the earlier Addenda A-C ran on an older commit of the scripts. Tested with stub apko, sudo and unshare. build/locks/apko.base.lock.json and apko-fips.base.lock.json are PLACEHOLDERS: their package entries (names, versions, ranges, checksums) were computed from the real Wolfi apks and match the live APKINDEX, but the config checksum is a marker and the file was not written by apko lock; the archive pull request regenerates them from a real archive. Wolfi's apks carry no per-package signature (the index is signed), so their signature entries are empty. Config fields outside the package list (accounts, paths, entrypoint, work-dir) are bound only by apko's own config-checksum check and by Rebuild's digest comparison; the base-vs-full comparison looks at package entries only. A wrong or unknown Wolfi key failing inside real apko is NOT proven by these tests (the keyring directory is pinned by digest instead); lock-proof.sh has no key case. Known residuals: the real apko image build is pending the runner proof; a forwarded-value echo in error messages is not escaped. Round-8 residuals: the '.'/'..' and control-character refusals are pinned for assemble-image.sh's own flags; lock-proof.sh and sealed-proof.sh pass their paths on to it.

## GUIDE

### REQ-GUIDE-001 — The v0.3.0 customer verification guide

The v0.3.0 customer verification guide (docs/verify-release.md) shall be one page of at most 500 words and at most 10 commands, using only cosign, gh and jq, that verifies signatures, digests, provenance, the SBOM and the inputs for both images (production and -fips); Witness records are extra evidence outside the ten commands; the page claims nothing the chain does not back; the owner reads it cold and a second reader tests it.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: v0.3.0 rule 78 (GUIDE-24); docs/verify-release.md; docs/verify-release.cannot-run.json; bin/verify-release-guide-test.sh*

> The command format is the one pipeline's AC7 run (bin/check-guide.sh, REQ-CHAIN-006-AC7) reads: a command is a line of a ```sh fenced block (a line ending in a backslash joins the next, so a continued command counts once; a pipeline counts once), a pipeline of cosign verify, cosign verify-attestation, cosign verify-blob, cosign verify-blob-attestation, gh attestation verify and jq with no other shell syntax. A verify command whose operand is an image reference (<IMAGE_REF>, <IMAGE_REF_FIPS>, oci://..., or a literal registry reference) needs a registry image and cannot run on a candidate, which Check holds as a file: it is listed, with its reason, in docs/verify-release.cannot-run.json, marked "Not run before release" on the page, and keeps the page from being final (AC7) until the owner decides rule 79's open case. The page test checks "in the order a customer runs them" only as "a file is verified before jq reads it"; the full order is judged by AC8's readers. The page is not linked from the README or any other page until v0.3.0 is live; docs/verify-images.md stays the guide for v0.2.x and gets a pointer to this page only when it is final.

## CI

### REQ-CI-001 — A required CI job that is split into parallel jobs runs every suite exactly once

When a required CI job of .github/workflows/ci.yml is split into parallel jobs to shorten the pull request wall time, no check is dropped and none runs twice: every step of the old job is in exactly one new job, unchanged, and a gate job with the old job's name, which the branch protection requires, fails unless every new job succeeded.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: ci-speed read-back of Oct 23 (advisor); the pin-wiring judge (pin-wiring-test.sh)*

> The pin-wiring judge accepts allowlist-chain in exactly two forms: the one job, or four parallel jobs plus the gate. The groups of suites per shard are fixed in the judge; moving a suite to another shard is a reviewed edit of the judge, which the trusted gate runs from main. The gate fails on a missing or empty result as on a failed, skipped or cancelled one.

| AC | Given / When / Then | Verification | Blocking | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-CI-001-AC1 | Given the CI workflow after a required job is split into parallel jobs; when the steps of the split jobs are compared with the steps the job had before the split; then every step of the old job is in exactly one of the new jobs, unchanged in name, run text and relative order, and no other step exists in them except the checkout, base-ref fetch, Python setup and pip steps each job needs | unit |  | approved | 1 item(s) |
| REQ-CI-001-AC2 | Given the same workflow; when the gate job is read; then a job with the old job's name exists, needs every new job, has `if: ${{ always() }}`, takes no checkout and no action, and exits non-zero unless the result of every needed job is exactly `success` (failed, skipped, cancelled, missing and empty each count as failure), so the required-check name is unchanged and a skipped shard cannot pass | unit |  | approved | 1 item(s) |
| REQ-CI-001-AC3 | Given any job of the split; when its keys are read; then no `if`, `env`, `continue-on-error`, `timeout-minutes`, `container`, `services`, `permissions`, `needs`, id-token or secret is added at job or step level, except the gate's own `needs`, `if` and the result variables of its one step | unit |  | approved | 1 item(s) |
| REQ-CI-001-AC4 | Given the pin-wiring judge; when it is run against a copy of the workflow with any one step dropped, duplicated across two jobs, moved, edited, reordered or conditioned, or with the gate weakened; then it fails for each of those mutations, and it accepts the real workflow | unit |  | approved | 1 item(s) |

### REQ-CI-005 — A floored suite is run once, by the step that counts it

Every suite named in test-evidence/suite-floors.json is run once per workflow run, by the step that runs it and counts its cases against its floor, and the step that re-runs the suites of the floors file runs only those that no counting step runs.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: ci-speed read-back of Oct 23 (advisor); the suite guard (bin/suite-guard-run.py); the pin-wiring judge (pin-wiring-test.sh)*

> A counting step is `python3 -I bin/suite-guard-run.py run test-evidence/suite-floors.json NAME PATH` (NAME the file name of PATH), which runs the suite once, shows its output as `bash PATH` would, requires exit 0 and a case count at or above the floor. The pin-wiring judge reads such a line back to the plain `bash PATH` line it stands for, so the exact-step checks are the same in both forms. `suite-guard-run.py all` skips the suites a trusted counting step runs (one line, the whole step, in a plain job that is a required check or is needed by one, one counting step per suite), runs the rest without echoing their output, and fails on a second counting step for one suite, on a ci.yml whose jobs are not a mapping, and on a counting step that names an unfloored suite, a floors file other than the committed one, or a NAME that is not the file name of its PATH. The floors only rise as before.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| REQ-CI-005-AC3 | Given a suite run by a counting step; when it loses cases (below its floor), prints no case count, or exits non-zero; then its step fails | unit |  | approved | 1 item(s) |
| REQ-CI-005-AC4 | Given the suite guard's floors; when a pull request lowers or drops a floor; then the floors-only-rise check fails as before; nothing in the counting step changes how a floor is raised | unit |  | approved | 1 item(s) |

Every other floored suite is counted by its own step and runs once. The count is of the steps of ci.yml; a suite that another suite runs inside itself (the matrix suite's variant harness) is not counted here | unit |  | approved | 1 item(s) |

### REQ-CI-006 — A sharded persona suite proves each case passed exactly once

If the persona suite is split across cores, the run first lists every case and then proves each case passed exactly once across the shards: none skipped, none doubled, none failed, no dead shard. The split is built only when the persona job is again the slowest CI job.

*Introduced v0.3.0 · tier community · confidence documented · source: ops/docs/ratify/2026-10-24-ci-suites-once-and-persona-shard.md*
